```text
5	
6	# models/issues — issues, pull requests, comments, reviews
7	
8	**Read when:** querying or changing issue, PR, comment, label, milestone or review rows.
9	**Not here:** the business logic on top -> `services/issue` and `services/pull`; project boards -> `models/project`.
10	
11	## Responsibilities
12	
13	One package for the whole issue domain, because pull requests *are* issues in this schema.
14	`models/pull` is separate and tiny: automerge scheduling and per-user review state.
15	
16	| Area | Files |
17	| --- | --- |
18	| Issue core | `issue.go`, `issue_list.go`, `issue_update.go`, `issue_search.go`, `issue_stats.go` |
19	| Pull requests | `pull.go`, `pull_list.go` |
20	| Comments | `comment.go`, `comment_list.go`, `comment_code.go`, `content_history.go` |
21	| Reviews | `review.go`, `review_list.go` |
22	| Labels / milestones | `issue_label.go`, `label.go`, `milestone.go`, `milestone_list.go` |
23	| People / time | `assignees.go`, `stopwatch.go`, `tracked_time.go` |
24	| Relations / state | `dependency.go`, `issue_xref.go`, `issue_watch.go`, `issue_pin.go`, `issue_lock.go`, `issue_user.go`, `issue_project.go`, `reaction.go` |
25	
26	## Key files
27	
28	| Path | What it holds |
29	| --- | --- |
30	| `models/issues/issue.go` | `Issue`, `ErrIssueNotExist`, `LoadRepo`, `LoadPullRequest`, `LoadAttributes` |
31	| `models/issues/issue_list.go` | `IssueList` and its batching `LoadAttributes` |
32	| `models/issues/pull.go` | `PullRequest`, `PullRequestType`, `PullRequestStatus` |
33	| `models/issues/comment.go` | `Comment` and the `CommentType` enum |
34	| `models/issues/issue_label.go` | `LoadLabels` — the idempotency pattern in miniature |
35	| `models/issues/issue_index.go` | `RecalculateIssueIndexForRepo` |
36	| `models/issues/issue_group.go` | `IssueLabelGroup`, `IssueList.GroupByExclusiveLabelScope` — the grouped list view |
37	
38	## Conventions & invariants
39	
40	- **One `issue` table holds both issues and pull requests.** `Issue.IsPull` discriminates. The
41	  PR-only columns live in a separate `PullRequest` row linked by `IssueID`, reachable via
42	  `issue.LoadPullRequest(ctx)` then `issue.PullRequest`. A query that forgets `IsPull` returns both
43	  kinds.
44	- `Issue.Index` is the **per-repository** number users see in URLs (`UNIQUE(repo_index)` with
45	  `RepoID`); `Issue.ID` is the global primary key. Look-ups by URL go through `RepoID` + `Index`.
46	- Never assign `Index` yourself: it comes from
47	  `db.GetNextResourceIndex(ctx, "issue_index", repo.ID)` inside the inserting transaction, as
48	  `issue_update.go` and `pull.go` do.
49	- Fields tagged `xorm:"-"` (`Repo`, `Poster`, `Labels`, `Milestone`, `Assignee`, `Attachments`,
50	  `Comments`, `PullRequest`, ...) are in-memory only, filled by the matching `LoadXxx(ctx)` method.
51	  `LoadAttributes(ctx)` loads the common set.
52	- `LoadXxx` methods are **idempotent and will not refresh**: each is guarded by an `isXxxLoaded`
53	  flag, so a second call is free — but a value that changed in the database after the first call
54	  stays stale on that struct. Re-fetch the issue rather than re-calling the loader.
55	- Error types come in the three-part shape: `ErrIssueNotExist` struct, `IsErrIssueNotExist(err)`,
56	  and `Unwrap() error` returning a `modules/util` sentinel such as `util.ErrNotExist`, so
57	  `errors.Is` works across layers.
58	- Comment kinds are the `CommentType` iota in `comment.go` (`CommentTypeComment` is a plain
59	  comment, `CommentTypeReview` a review, plus many state-change kinds). Rendering branches on it —
60	  adding a value means handling it in the templates too.
```

```text
147	## Traps, and what they look like
148	
149	**A database test fails with something about a nil or closed connection.** The package is missing
150	its `main_test.go`, so no test database was ever built.
151	
152	**Your test passes alone and fails in the full run.** Either it is missing
153	`unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()`, or an earlier test left state behind. Integration and browser
154	tests share one Gitea instance for the whole run, so a test that creates something and does not
155	clean up breaks a *later* test, not itself — the failure points at innocent code.
156	
157	**`CheckConsistencyFor` fails in a test you did not write.** You added or changed a fixture row and
158	a counter column no longer matches.
159	
160	**A browser test only passes when you raise `GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR`.** That multiplier
161	defaults to 4 on CI and 1 locally. Needing more is a flaky test — usually waiting on the wrong
162	thing — not a slow laptop. Fix the wait, do not raise the number.
163	
164	**A handful of Go tests fail on Windows** for symlink and temp-file reasons that are not your bug.
165	Run the suite on Linux, macOS, WSL2 or the provided `.devcontainer`.
166	
167	**You cannot tell what a failing database test actually did.** Set `GITEA_TEST_LOG_SQL=1` and it
168	prints every SQL statement it ran. This is the fastest debugging tool here.
169
```

```text
44	outside the transaction.** No error, no warning. It just does not roll back.
45	
46	## Words you'll meet
47	
48	- **engine** — the database connection. `db.GetEngine(ctx)` gives you one.
49	- **transaction** — a group of writes that all succeed or all get undone.
50	- **roll back** — undoing a transaction's writes because something failed.
51	- **bean** — a Go struct mapping to a table. Gitea's database library calls them beans.
52	- **register a model** — telling the library that a struct is a table.
53	- **generic helper** — a function working for any bean type, written `db.GetByID[T]`.
54	- **atomic** — all-or-nothing.
55	- **`WHERE` clause** — the part of an SQL statement saying *which* rows. Leaving it off means all
56	  of them.
57	
58	## What's in these files
59	
60	| Where | What it is for |
61	| --- | --- |
62	| `models/db/context.go` | The core. `GetEngine`, `WithTx`, `WithTx2`, `Insert`, and the generic lookups. |
63	| `models/db/engine.go` | `RegisterModel`, plus table-level utilities and SQL logging. |
64	| `models/db/engine_init.go` | Building the connection at startup. |
65	| `models/db/list.go` | Pagination: `ListOptions`, `FindOptions`. |
66	| `models/db/index.go` | `GetNextResourceIndex` — per-parent numbering, which is how per-repo issue numbers work. |
67	| `models/db/iterate.go` | Streaming through a result set too large to hold in memory. |
68	| `models/db/error.go` | The database-level error types. |
69	| `models/db/install/` | Database setup during first-run installation. |
70	
71	## The rules, and why
72	
73	**Always take `ctx` as the first parameter, and get the engine from it.** Never keep an engine in a
74	struct field, and never accept a session object as a parameter. This is what makes transactions
75	propagate; break it and they stop working with no visible symptom.
76	
77	**`db.GetEngine(ctx)` is the whole mechanism.** Inside a transaction it returns that transaction's
78	session; outside, the shared connection. So a helper that is handed the wrong `ctx` — a background
79	one, or one from an outer scope — quietly writes outside the transaction and cannot be rolled back.
80	When you read a function, checking which `ctx` it passes on is the single most useful thing to look
81	at.
82	
83	**Writes that must succeed together go inside `db.WithTx`.** Use `db.WithTx2` when the block needs
84	to return a value as well as an error.
85	
86	**Every stored struct registers itself.** In the file declaring it, an `init()` calls
87	`db.RegisterModel(new(Foo))`. 101 files under `models/` do this — copy whichever one you are next
88	to.
89	
90	**Prefer the generic helpers** — `db.GetByID[T]`, `db.Exist[T]`, `db.DeleteByID[T]` — over
91	hand-written engine calls. They already apply the right conditions and error handling, and a
92	hand-rolled equivalent usually forgets one.
93	
94	**Never update without a `WHERE`.** An update with no condition rewrites *every row in the table*.
95	This is the most destructive mistake available in this package, and the database will do it without
96	complaint.
97	
98	**Fields tagged `xorm:"-"` are not columns.** They exist only in memory, filled in by Go code. They
99	are never read from or written to the database, so setting one and saving the struct changes
100	nothing.
101	
102	## How to actually do it
```

```text
44	## Words you'll meet
45	
46	- **discriminator** — a column saying which kind of thing a row is. Here, `IsPull`.
47	- **primary key** — the globally unique `ID`.
48	- **per-repository index** — the number users see (`#42`), which restarts at 1 in every repository.
49	- **loader** — a `LoadXxx(ctx)` method that fills in one of those empty fields.
50	- **idempotent** — calling it twice does the same as calling it once.
51	- **denormalised counter** — a count stored on another row for speed, which then has to be kept
52	  correct by hand.
53	- **N+1** — fetching *n* things and then running *n* more queries, one per item.
54	- **sentinel error** — a shared error value that code elsewhere can test for.
55	
56	## What's in these files
57	
58	| Where | What it is for |
59	| --- | --- |
60	| `models/issues/issue.go` | The `Issue` struct itself, its loaders, and its "not found" error. |
61	| `models/issues/issue_list.go` | `IssueList` — a slice of issues that can load everything for all of them at once. |
62	| `models/issues/pull.go` | The pull-request-only row. |
63	| `models/issues/comment.go` | Comments, and the enum of comment kinds. |
64	| `models/issues/issue_label.go` | Labels on issues — and the clearest small example of the loader pattern. |
65	| `models/issues/issue_index.go` | Recalculating per-repository numbering. |
66	| `models/issues/issue_group.go` | Splitting a list of issues into category groups, for the grouped ("folder") list view. |
67	
68	The rest divide by area: `review.go` and `review_list.go`, `label.go`, `milestone.go`,
69	`assignees.go`, `stopwatch.go` and `tracked_time.go`, and the relationship files `dependency.go`,
70	`issue_xref.go`, `issue_watch.go`, `issue_pin.go`, `issue_lock.go`, `reaction.go`.
71	
72	## The rules, and why
73	
74	**`IsPull` decides what a row is.** A query that forgets it returns both issues and pull requests.
75	On an issues page that means pull requests appearing in the list; on a count, a number that is
76	always too high.
77	
78	**`Index` is not `ID`.** `ID` is the global primary key. `Index` is the number in the URL, unique
79	only *within* a repository — so every repository has an issue `#1`. Looking something up from a URL
80	means matching on the repository **and** the index. Using the URL number as an `ID` finds a
81	completely unrelated issue in another repository, which is worse than an error because it looks like
82	it worked.
83	
84	**Never set `Index` yourself.** It comes from the shared numbering helper, called inside the same
85	transaction that inserts the row. Assigning it by hand races with anyone else creating an issue in
86	that repository at the same moment.
87	
88	**Fields tagged `xorm:"-"` are empty until you load them.** `Repo`, `Poster`, `Labels`,
89	`Milestone`, `Assignee`, `Attachments`, `Comments`, `PullRequest` and others are all filled in by a
90	matching `LoadXxx(ctx)` method. `LoadAttributes(ctx)` loads the usual set in one go.
91	
92	**Loaders never refresh.** Each is guarded by an internal "already loaded" flag, so calling one
93	twice is free — but it also means a value that changed in the database after the first call **stays
94	stale on that struct**. If you need current data, re-fetch the issue; calling the loader again does
95	nothing.
96	
97	**Errors come in three parts.** There is an `ErrIssueNotExist` struct, an `IsErrIssueNotExist(err)`
98	test, and an `Unwrap()` that returns a shared sentinel like `util.ErrNotExist`. That third part is
99	what lets a handler ask "is this a not-found error?" without importing every model package — and it
100	is what turns a missing issue into a 404 instead of a 500.
101	
102	**Comment kinds are an enum**, and rendering branches on it. A plain comment and a review are both
103	comments with different kinds, as are all the "closed this", "added a label" timeline entries.
104	Adding a kind means handling it in the templates too, or it renders as nothing.
105
```

The docs commit (`fa8b5361b3`) landed and the tree is clean. Here's the plan for commit 2. It stays in the model layer and doesn't change any existing behaviour: nothing calls the new code until commit 3.

### Commit 2: the reason rules, with no database access

**Where:** `models/issues/issue_close_reason.go` (extended) and its test file.

```go
func AllowedCloseReasons(isPull bool) []CloseReason     // issue: all 4; PR: no "completed"

type CloseReasonOptions struct {                        // what a person gives when closing
	Reason CloseReason
	Text   string // only for CloseReasonOther
}
func (opts CloseReasonOptions) Validate(isPull bool) error

type ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed struct{ ... }             // AC5, and any out-of-range number
type ErrInvalidCloseReasonText struct{ ... }            // AC3: empty after trim, or over 255 chars
```

1. **`AllowedCloseReasons`** is the list #54 will build its dropdown from. A PR doesn't get "completed", because a PR completes by being merged (AC5).
2. **`CloseReasonOptions`** is one value that commit 3 passes from the service down to the comment, instead of loose parameters threaded through four functions. Commit 4 adds the duplicate target to it.
3. **`Validate` checks, in order:**
   - `CloseReasonNone` passes. That's the no-reason path every existing caller uses (AC7).
   - A reason outside the list for an issue or a PR is rejected. This also catches values like `99`, which the database won't stop (the enum convention we just documented).
   - For "other", text that's empty after trimming is rejected (Decision 2), and so is text over 255 characters. Characters are counted with `utf8.RuneCountInString`, because Go's `len()` counts bytes and would reject 200 accented letters. The text is stored as entered, per AC3.
4. **The two errors follow the three-part shape from `models-issues.md`:** a struct, an `IsErrXxx(err)` check, and `Unwrap()` returning `util.ErrInvalidArgument`. That value carries the "implies HTTP 400" comment in `modules/util/error.go`, and `review.go` already uses it the same way, so #55 gets the right status code for free.

**Tests:** table-driven unit tests with no database:
- The PR list lacks "completed", and the issue list has all four.
- `None` is accepted, and each allowed reason is accepted.
- A PR closed as "completed" and the value `99` are both rejected.
- Empty and whitespace-only text are rejected.
- 255 characters pass and 256 fail, including a 255-character accented string, which would fail if bytes were counted.
- Each error satisfies `errors.Is(err, util.ErrInvalidArgument)`.

**Docs:** probably none this time, because commit 2 follows conventions that are already written down.

### One decision before I write it

What should happen when text arrives with a reason other than "other", say "completed" plus text?
- **Reject it with `ErrInvalidCloseReasonText` (my recommendation).** A client that sends it has a bug, and rejecting keeps "text only for other" true in the data. The cost is that #54's form has to clear the text box when the dropdown changes.
- **Drop the text silently.** That's more forgiving, but a buggy client never finds out its text was discarded.

Commit 2 stays in the model layer, one step up from the database. It adds the **rules** for what counts as a valid close reason. It writes nothing to the database, and nothing calls it yet.

```
 browser / API                                  ← #54, #55
      │
 routers                                        read the request
      │
 services/issue/status.go    CloseIssue         ← commit 3: take a reason, check it, pass it down
      │
 models/issues/
   issue_close_reason.go                        ← commit 2 (NEXT): the rules for a valid reason
   issue_update.go                              ← commit 3: write the reason into the row
      │
 database: issue table                          ← commit 1 (DONE): the columns exist, nothing fills them
```

**Where things stand:** after commit 1, the database *can* hold a reason, but nothing ever writes one.

**What commit 2 changes:** one file, `models/issues/issue_close_reason.go`, gets four things added:
- **The allowed list:** issues can use all four reasons, and PRs every reason except "completed".
- **A small struct** that bundles the reason with its "other" text, so it travels as one value.
- **A check function** that answers whether a reason is valid for this issue or PR.
- **Two error types** that say why a reason was refused.

In TypeScript terms, it's like writing a zod schema before wiring it into any route handler.

**Why this is needed:** the database can't enforce these rules, because it only stores numbers and text. So something in Go has to refuse "completed" on a PR, or empty "other" text. Commit 3 will call this check before closing, so a bad reason is rejected and the issue stays open (AC3, AC5).

**Why the model layer and not the service layer:** these are rules about which values are legal for the data. Gitea keeps that kind of rule and its errors next to the model: `ErrIssueNotExist` and `ErrDependenciesLeft` both live in `models/issues`. Keeping it there also means #54's dropdown can read the same allowed list instead of keeping a copy.

**The one decision it needs, in plain terms:** if someone picks "completed" and also sends some "other" text, should the check refuse the close, or quietly throw the text away? I'd refuse it, so a buggy form or API client finds out. Throwing it away is more forgiving but hides the bug.

```markdown
# Issue #53 — design decisions

### Decision 5: Reject text sent with any reason other than "other"

**Decision:** Closing with "completed", "not planned", "duplicate" or no reason while also sending text is rejected with `ErrInvalidCloseReasonText`, rather than the text being dropped. Whitespace-only text still counts as no text (Decision 2).
**Alternatives Considered:** Silently discard the text and close with the chosen reason.
**Rationale:** A close carries exactly one reason, and text belongs only to "other". A form or API client that sends both has a bug; rejecting tells it so, while discarding hides the bug and loses what the person typed.
**Consequences:** The close form in #54 has to clear the text box when a reason other than "other" is picked, and API clients in #55 get a 400 if they send both.
```

```go
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issues

import (
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"gitea.dev/modules/util"
)

// CloseReason records why an issue or pull request was closed.
// It is stored as an integer, so existing values must never be renumbered.
type CloseReason int

const (
	CloseReasonNone       CloseReason = iota // 0
	CloseReasonCompleted                     // 1
	CloseReasonNotPlanned                    // 2
	CloseReasonDuplicate                     // 3
	CloseReasonOther                         // 4
)

// CloseReasonTextMaxLength matches the VARCHAR(255) close_reason_text column, counted in characters.
const CloseReasonTextMaxLength = 255

// AllowedCloseReasons lists the reasons a person can pick when closing.
// A pull request is completed by merging, so it cannot be closed as completed.
func AllowedCloseReasons(isPull bool) []CloseReason {
	if isPull {
		return []CloseReason{CloseReasonNotPlanned, CloseReasonDuplicate, CloseReasonOther}
	}
	return []CloseReason{CloseReasonCompleted, CloseReasonNotPlanned, CloseReasonDuplicate, CloseReasonOther}
}

// CloseReasonOptions is the reason a person gives when closing an issue or pull request.
type CloseReasonOptions struct {
	Reason CloseReason
	Text   string // only for CloseReasonOther
}

// Validate checks the options for an issue or pull request.
// CloseReasonNone is always valid, so close paths that give no reason keep working.
func (opts CloseReasonOptions) Validate(isPull bool) error {
	if opts.Reason != CloseReasonNone && !slices.Contains(AllowedCloseReasons(isPull), opts.Reason) {
		return ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed{Reason: opts.Reason, IsPull: isPull}
	}

	hasText := strings.TrimSpace(opts.Text) != "" // whitespace-only counts as no text
	if opts.Reason != CloseReasonOther {
		if hasText {
			return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: "text is only allowed with the other reason"}
		}
		return nil
	}
	if !hasText {
		return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: "text is empty"}
	}
	if utf8.RuneCountInString(opts.Text) > CloseReasonTextMaxLength {
		return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: fmt.Sprintf("text is longer than %d characters", CloseReasonTextMaxLength)}
	}
	return nil
}

// ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed represents a reason that is out of range, or not allowed for the issue or pull request.
type ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed struct {
	Reason CloseReason
	IsPull bool
}

// IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed checks if an error is a ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed.
func IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed(err error) bool {
	_, ok := err.(ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed)
	return ok
}

func (err ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("close reason is not allowed for this %s [reason: %d]", util.Iif(err.IsPull, "pull request", "issue"), err.Reason)
}

func (err ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed) Unwrap() error {
	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
}

// ErrInvalidCloseReasonText represents close reason text that is empty, too long, or sent with a reason other than CloseReasonOther.
type ErrInvalidCloseReasonText struct {
	Reason CloseReason
	Detail string
}

// IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText checks if an error is a ErrInvalidCloseReasonText.
func IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText(err error) bool {
	_, ok := err.(ErrInvalidCloseReasonText)
	return ok
}

func (err ErrInvalidCloseReasonText) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("invalid close reason text: %s [reason: %d]", err.Detail, err.Reason)
}

func (err ErrInvalidCloseReasonText) Unwrap() error {
	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
}

```

Commit 2 is ready for you to commit. It's two files in the model layer, and nothing calls the new code yet.

**`models/issues/issue_close_reason.go`** now holds four things below the constants:
- **`AllowedCloseReasons(isPull)`**: issues can use all four reasons, PRs everything except "completed".
- **`CloseReasonOptions`**: the reason and its "other" text, bundled into one value.
- **`Validate(isPull)`**, which checks in this order:
  - "No reason" always passes, so existing close paths keep working.
  - A reason that isn't allowed for this issue or PR is refused. That includes nonsense numbers like `99`.
  - Text sent with a reason other than "other" is refused (Decision 5).
  - "Other" text is refused if it's empty after trimming or longer than 255 characters, counted as characters rather than bytes.
- **`ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed`** and **`ErrInvalidCloseReasonText`**, written in the same shape as `ErrNotValidReviewRequest` in `review.go`. Both unwrap to `util.ErrInvalidArgument`, so the API will return a 400.
- **`CloseReasonTextMaxLength = 255`**, so #54 can use the same number for the text box's limit instead of repeating it.

One behaviour that follows from Decisions 2 and 5: whitespace-only text sent with, say, "completed" counts as no text, so it passes rather than being refused. There's a test case for it.

**`issue_close_reason_test.go`** adds 17 unit cases with no database. I checked they catch the two likeliest mistakes: counting bytes with `len()` fails the 255 accented-character case, and dropping the "no reason" exemption fails three cases. My first attempt at the byte-count check didn't compile, so it tested nothing; I reran it properly.

**Checks:** all tests pass, the full `models/issues` suite passes, `make fmt` made no stray changes, the scoped lint reports `0 issues`, and whitespace is clean. Decision 5 is in `.specstory/issue-53-design-decisions.md` for you to paste.

```text
func (c *Comment) MetaSpecialDoerTr(locale translation.Locale) template.HTML {
	if c.CommentMetaData == nil {

func CreateComment(ctx context.Context, opts *CreateCommentOptions) (_ *Comment, err error) {
	return db.WithTx2(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) (*Comment, error) {
		var LabelID int64
```

```bash
func TestCloseIssueRecordsReason(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name     string
		reason   issues_model.CloseReasonOptions
		wantText string
	}{
		{name: "no reason", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{}},
		{name: "completed", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonCompleted}},
		{name: "other with text", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: "superseded"}, wantText: "superseded"},
		{name: "whitespace-only text is not stored", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonNotPlanned, Text: " "}},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
			issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
			doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})

			comment, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(t.Context(), issue, doer, c.reason)
			require.NoError(t, err)

			want := issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: c.reason.Reason, Text: c.wantText}
			issue = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
			assert.True(t, issue.IsClosed)
			assert.Equal(t, want, issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issue.CloseReason, Text: issue.CloseReasonText})

			comment = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{ID: comment.ID}) // reloaded, so the metadata went through JSON
			assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CommentTypeClose, comment.Type)
			assert.Equal(t, want, comment.MetaCloseReason())
		})
	}
}

func TestCloseIssueInvalidReasonLeavesItOpen(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name    string
		issueID int64
		reason  issues_model.CloseReasonOptions
		isErr   func(error) bool
	}{
		{name: "pull request closed as completed", issueID: 2, reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonCompleted}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed},
		{name: "other with no text", issueID: 1, reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
			issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: c.issueID})
			doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})

			_, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(t.Context(), issue, doer, c.reason)
			assert.True(t, c.isErr(err), "unexpected error: %v", err)
			assert.False(t, issue.IsClosed, "the in-memory issue must not be changed either")

			issue = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: c.issueID})
			assert.False(t, issue.IsClosed)
			assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonNone, issue.CloseReason)
			unittest.AssertNotExistsBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{IssueID: c.issueID, Type: issues_model.CommentTypeClose})
		})
	}
}
EOF
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-27 20:32:26Z)**_

Commit 3 is ready for you to commit. It's the first commit that changes behaviour: closing can now record a reason, and every existing close path still records none.

```
 routers (web, API)                   unchanged: they still call CloseIssue, so they close with no reason
      │
 services/issue/status.go             CloseIssue → now a wrapper; CloseIssueWithReason does the work
      │
 models/issues/issue_update.go        SetIssueAsClosed: check the reason → write it to the issue row
 models/issues/comment.go             …and copy it into the close comment's metadata
      │
 database                             issue.close_reason*, comment.comment_meta_data (JSON)
```

### What changed, by layer

**Service (`services/issue/status.go`).**
- `CloseIssueWithReason` holds the old body and passes the reason down.
- `CloseIssue` is now a one-line wrapper that passes no reason, as you asked. I kept its original `// CloseIssue close an issue.` line and added the backwards-compatibility explanation below it.

**Model: closing (`models/issues/issue_update.go`).**
- `SetIssueAsClosed` takes a reason and checks it before anything is written (Decision 6, now in the decisions file).
- It then saves the reason on the issue row. The text is saved only for "other", because `Validate` lets whitespace-only text through with other reasons.
- The reason is copied onto the new comment only for a plain close. Merge and reopen comments share the same function, and reopen doesn't clear the issue's reason until commit 5, so without this they would pick up the stale reason.

**Model: the comment (`models/issues/comment.go`).**
- `CommentMetaData` gets `CloseReason` and `CloseReasonText`, following Decision 4.
- `CreateComment` fills them in when a reason is given.
- `MetaCloseReason()` reads them back safely. A comment without metadata, which includes every close comment that existed before this change, reads as "no reason". This is modelled on the existing `MetaSpecialDoerTr`, and #54's templates will need it, since a template errors on a nil field.

**Other files.**
- `services/pull/merge.go` now passes an empty reason explicitly, so "a merge records no reason" is visible at the call site.
- Two existing tests (`issue_xref_test.go`, `dependency_test.go`) needed the new argument.

### Checks

- **New tests:** two table tests with six cases, covering AC2 and AC7, and AC3/AC5's "the issue stays open, in the database and in memory, and no close comment is created". I broke the three riskiest lines one at a time and each break failed a test.
- **Existing tests:** the full suites for `models/issues`, `services/issue` and `services/pull` pass, and so do three existing integration tests, one for each close path this commit touches: `TestIssueCommentClose` (web), `TestAPIIssue` (API) and `TestPullMerge` (merge). I confirmed with `-v` that they actually ran.
- `make fmt` and the scoped lint are clean, and whitespace is fine.

```
git add models/issues/comment.go models/issues/issue_update.go models/issues/issue_close_reason_test.go models/issues/issue_xref_test.go models/issues/dependency_test.go services/issue/status.go services/pull/merge.go
```

```
Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5
```

**Next,** I'd do commit 4 (duplicate), then commit 5 (reopen), so the reason struct is complete before any router uses it. After that, the web close path gets its reason from the form, per Decision 1, leaving the API to #55. I'd then do a single docs pass for commits 2–5, unless you want the docs now.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Gitea's MSSQL default string type is nvarchar, so VARCHAR(255) becomes NVARCHAR(255), which counts UTF-16 units rather than characters—meaning 255 emoji could pass validation but still overflow only on MSSQL. I'll check whether Gitea's own 255-character title limit shares this issue before deciding if it matters.

</details></think>

The review found nothing broken in commits 1–3. There's one wrong code comment, and the docs are behind the code. Here are the results and the cleanup I'd make; nothing is changed yet.

### Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Every `models` package, run in parallel | All non-migration packages pass. Two old `v1_14` migration tests failed on a shared repo directory disappearing mid-test |
| The same migration packages, one at a time (`make migrations.individual.test`, as the Makefile runs them) | All 15 pass, including those two, so parallel runs caused the failures, not our change |
| `services/issue` and `services/pull` suites, plus the web, API and merge integration tests (commit 3) | Pass |
| `go build ./...`, scoped lint, `make fmt`, whitespace, `check.sh` | Clean |
| Every caller of the changed signatures | Compiles; the only outside caller is `merge.go` |

### Proposed cleanup

1. **The comment on `CloseIssue` in `services/issue/status.go` is inaccurate.** It lists "merged … pull requests" among its callers, but a PR's own merge calls the model directly (`merge.go:720`). What goes through `CloseIssue` is *issues that a merged PR references* (`handleCloseCrossReferences`), plus PRs whose branch was deleted (`pull.go`). It's a one-line fix, so the comment doesn't send anyone looking for the wrong path.

```text
## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `services/issue/issue.go` | `NewIssue`, `ChangeTitle`, `ChangeIssueRef`, `ChangeTimeEstimate`, `DeleteIssue` |
| `services/issue/label.go` | `AddLabel`, `AddLabels`, `RemoveLabel`, `ReplaceLabels`, `ClearLabels` |
| `services/issue/assignee.go` | `ToggleAssignee`, `AddAssignees`, `RemoveAssignees`, `UpdateAssignees` |
| `services/issue/content.go` | `ChangeContent` |
| `services/issue/status.go` | open/close transitions |
| `services/issue/comments.go`, `reaction.go`, `milestone.go` | comment, reaction and milestone operations |
| `services/issue/review_request.go` | `ReviewRequest`, `TeamReviewRequest`, `CanDoerChangeReviewRequests` |
| `services/issue/commit.go` | `UpdateIssuesCommit` — acts on `fixes #123` in pushed commit messages |
| `services/issue/template.go` | issue template parsing |
| `services/issue/suggestion.go` | `GetSuggestion` for the issue autocomplete |

## Conventions & invariants

- Signature shape is `(ctx, issue, doer, ...)`. `doer` is who is acting — it is required, because
  it lands on the timeline comment and on the notification. Do not add a function that mutates an
  issue without a doer.
- **Order of operations, and it matters:**
  1. Load what you need (`issue.LoadRepo(ctx)`, `LoadPoster`) — see `models-issues.md` on loaders.
  2. Refuse blocked users with `user_model.IsUserBlockedBy` *before* mutating.
  3. Mutate inside `db.WithTx`, delegating the row writes to `models/issues`.
  4. **After the transaction returns**, call `notify_service.*`.
- That last point is the invariant to protect: `notify_service` calls sit outside `db.WithTx` in
  `NewIssue` and everywhere else. Notifications send mail, fire webhooks and write UI
  notifications; doing that inside a transaction that later rolls back tells users about something
  that never happened. Never move a notify call inside the tx.
- The import alias is always `notify_service "gitea.dev/services/notify"`.
- A state change is recorded as a `Comment` row with the matching `CommentType`, not just a field
  update. The issue timeline *is* those comment rows, so a mutation that skips the comment leaves
  no history.
```

```text
- `ChangeContent` takes a `contentVersion` for optimistic concurrency — pass the version the client
  submitted, do not invent one.

## Recipes

**Add a new issue mutation.** Write the row change in `models/issues` first, then a thin function
here that does the four steps above. Look at `ChangeTitle` as the smallest complete example: load,
block-check, model call, `notify_service.IssueChangeTitle`.

**Act on a new commit-message keyword.** `UpdateIssuesCommit` in `commit.go`, which runs from the
push path (`services-repository.md`). Reference parsing itself is in `modules/references`.

**Add a timeline entry for something new.** Add a `CommentType` value in `models/issues`, create
the comment in your service function, and handle the new type in the issue-view templates —
an unhandled type renders as nothing.

## Gotchas

- Calling a `models/issues` function directly from a router skips every check in this package:
  blocked users, the timeline comment and the notification. Routers call services, not models.
- `NewIssue` here differs from `issues_model.NewIssue` in `models/issues` by exactly this wrapper.
  Import-alias the two (`issue_service` / `issues_model`) so the call site says which one you mean.
- Counter columns on `Repository` are maintained by the model layer; if you write a mutation that
  bypasses it, `unittest.CheckConsistencyFor` will fail (`testing.md`).

## Related

- `models-issues.md` — the rows and their loaders
- `services-pull-and-gitdiff.md` — the PR-side equivalents, including reviews
- `routers-web.md`, `routers-api-v1.md` — the callers
```

```text
func (comments CommentList) loadDependentIssues(ctx context.Context) error {
	if len(comments) == 0 {
		return nil
	}

	e := db.GetEngine(ctx)
	issueIDs := comments.getDependentIssueIDs()
	if len(issueIDs) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	issues := make(map[int64]*Issue, len(issueIDs))
	left := len(issueIDs)
	for left > 0 {
		limit := min(left, db.DefaultMaxInSize)
		rows, err := e.
			In("id", issueIDs[:limit]).
			Rows(new(Issue))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		for rows.Next() {
			var issue Issue
			err = rows.Scan(&issue)
			if err != nil {
				_ = rows.Close()
				return err
			}

			issues[issue.ID] = &issue
		}
		_ = rows.Close()

		left -= limit
		issueIDs = issueIDs[limit:]
	}

	for _, comment := range comments {
		if comment.DependentIssue == nil {
			comment.DependentIssue = issues[comment.DependentIssueID]
			if comment.DependentIssue != nil {
				if err := comment.DependentIssue.LoadRepo(ctx); err != nil {
					return err
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return nil
}
```

Commit 4 finishes AC4: closing as "duplicate of #12". It extends the pieces commits 2 and 3 built, so it's the same layers again, plus one small step up into the web layer that I need you to decide on.

```
 routers/web/repo/issue_view.go     ← (decision below) load the target when the timeline is shown
      │
 services/issue                     unchanged: CloseIssueWithReason already passes the options down
      │
 models/issues/
   issue_close_reason.go            ← the number typed by the person, and the rules that need no database
   issue_update.go                  ← look the number up in this repo, save the target's ID
   comment.go                       ← the close comment keeps the target ID, and can load that issue
      │
 database                           issue.close_duplicate_issue_id (column from commit 1, unused until now)
```

### What changes, and why

1. **The input.** `CloseReasonOptions` gets `DuplicateIndex`, the number the person types (#12). That's the per-repo number, not the internal ID.

2. **Rules that need no database**, added to `Validate`:
   - "duplicate" requires a number.
   - A number sent with any other reason is refused, following the same one-reason contract as Decision 5.

3. **Rules that need the database**, in `SetIssueAsClosed`, inside the close transaction as Decision 6 planned:
   - The number must not be the issue's own.
   - It must exist in the same repository. The lookup uses `GetIssueByIndex(repoID, number)`, so a #12 that exists only in some other repo is refused.
   - On success, the target's global ID is stored on the issue (Decision 3) and copied into the close comment's metadata.
   - All three failures (missing, self, not found) use one new error with a detail message. It unwraps to "invalid argument", so the API returns a 400, like the other two errors.

4. **Loading the target for display.** AC4 says the close comment "has the target issue loaded (number, title, link)".
   - The comment only stores an ID, so it gets a loader, `LoadCloseDuplicateIssue`. It's copied from the dependency comments' `LoadDepIssueDetails`, which does the same job for "added a dependency on #N".
   - If the target is later deleted, loading reports "not found" and the page still renders. The dependency branch in `issue_view.go` handles it the same way.

Two behaviours follow from the AC's wording, and I'll implement them this way unless you object:
- **Any issue or PR in the same repo can be the target.** Issues and PRs share one set of numbers, and AC4 doesn't restrict the kind.
- **A closed target is fine.** Duplicates of closed issues are common.

The tests cover each rule, the stored ID on both the issue and the comment, and the loader.

### The one decision: should the issue page load the target in this commit?

- **Yes, in `issue_view.go` (my recommendation).** I'd add a six-line branch next to the existing dependency branch, which is where every other comment type's linked data gets loaded. AC4 is then fully true in #53, and #54 only has to touch templates. The cost is a tiny router change, plus one extra lookup per close-as-duplicate comment that nothing displays until #54.
- **No, only the model loader now.** #53 stays out of routers entirely, and #54 adds the call along with the template. The cost is that AC4's "has the target loaded" is only true once #54 lands.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-27 21:29:43Z)**_

The duplicate target makes two lookups, one in each direction, and Gitea already has a precedent for each. When someone closes the issue, the number they typed is turned into the target issue. When the page is shown later, the stored ID is turned back into that issue.

```
WRITE: closing as a duplicate
 person types 12 ─► router builds CloseReasonOptions{Reason: Duplicate, DuplicateIndex: 12}
   ─► CloseIssueWithReason ─► issues_model.CloseIssue ─► SetIssueAsClosed   (inside the transaction)
        Validate: is there a number, and only with "duplicate"?
        is 12 this issue's own number?                  → refuse
        GetIssueByIndex(this repo, 12)                  → not found: refuse
        found: that issue's global ID is, say, 4711
   ─► issue row:     close_duplicate_issue_id = 4711
   ─► close comment: metadata {close_reason: 3, close_duplicate_issue_id: 4711}

READ: showing the issue page
 issue_view.go, for each close comment ─► LoadCloseDuplicateIssue
   ─► GetIssueByID(4711) ─► comment.CloseDuplicateIssue = #12, its title, its Link()
   ─► template (#54) renders "closed as duplicate of #12"
```

**Number → issue** uses `GetIssueByIndex(repoID, number)`, the same call Gitea uses wherever a person gives a number:
- Opening `/issues/12`: `routers/web/repo/issue.go`.
- `fixes #12` in a pushed commit: `services/issue/commit.go`.
- The issue being edited on the dependency route: `routers/web/repo/issue_dependency.go`.

The repo ID is part of that lookup, so "same repository" (AC4) comes built in.

**Storing the ID and loading by ID** matches every other link between issues on `Comment`:
- `DependentIssueID` is read back by `LoadDepIssueDetails` with `GetIssueByID`.
- `RefIssueID`, the "mentioned this in #N" entries, is read back the same way in `models/issues/issue_xref.go`.

The number is what people see but only means something inside one repo, while the ID is unique everywhere.

**The one place that works differently: adding a dependency.** That form sends an ID, not a number (`ctx.FormInt64("newDependency")` → `GetIssueByID`), because the person picks the issue from a search dropdown. An ID can belong to any repository, so the handler has to check separately: `if issue.RepoID != dep.RepoID`. If #54 wants a search dropdown for duplicates, I'd still have it send the number, since each search result has one. The model then keeps "number in, same-repo check for free", and #55's API can take the number the way GitHub's does.

If that matches what you had in mind, I'll implement commit 4 as described, with the `issue_view.go` branch included.

```text
func GetIssueByIndex(ctx context.Context, repoID, index int64) (*Issue, error) {
	if index < 1 {

	}
```

```markdown
# Issue #53 — design decisions

### Decision 7: The duplicate target is given as its number in the repository, and stored as its ID

**Decision:** A close as duplicate takes the number people see (`#12`, `DuplicateIndex`), looks it up with `GetIssueByIndex(repoID, number)` inside the close transaction, and stores the target's global ID on the issue and in the close comment's metadata. Any issue or pull request with that number in the same repository can be the target, open or closed; the issue itself and numbers that exist only in other repositories are rejected with `ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate`.
**Alternatives Considered:** Take the target's global ID, picked from a search dropdown, the way adding a dependency does (`routers/web/repo/issue_dependency.go`).
**Rationale:** Looking up by repository and number is how Gitea resolves every number a person gives (issue URLs, `fixes #12` in commits), and it keeps the target in the same repository without a separate check. The dependency form takes an ID, so it has to compare repositories itself. Storing the ID matches every other link between issues (`DependentIssueID`, `RefIssueID`), because a number only means something within one repository.
**Consequences:** Cross-repository duplicates are not possible, as AC4 intends. A search dropdown in #54 has to send the number, not the ID. Reading the target back takes a separate lookup by ID, and a deleted target shows up as "not found" rather than an error.

### Decision 8: The issue page loads the duplicate target in this issue, not in #54

**Decision:** `routers/web/repo/issue_view.go` calls `Comment.LoadCloseDuplicateIssue` for close comments, in the same place and the same way it loads the issue named by a dependency comment, and tolerates a deleted target.
**Alternatives Considered:** Add only the model loader in #53, and let #54 call it together with the template that shows it.
**Rationale:** AC4 says the close comment has the target issue loaded (number, title, link). Loading it where every other comment type's linked data is loaded makes that true within #53, and leaves #54 with template work only.
**Consequences:** Until #54 renders it, each close-as-duplicate comment costs one extra lookup when the issue page is viewed. Close comments without a duplicate return before any lookup.

```

```bash
func TestReopenIssueClearsReason(t *testing.T) {

	}{

	}
	for _, c := range cases {

			issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
			doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})

			closeComment, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(t.Context(), issue, doer, c.reason)
			require.NoError(t, err)

			assert.Equal(t, c.reason.Reason, closeComment.MetaCloseReason().Reason, "the close comment keeps its reason")

			require.NoError(t, closeComment.LoadCloseDuplicateIssue(t.Context()))

			assert.Nil(t, reopenComment.CommentMetaData)

	}
}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-27 21:51:20Z)**_

Yes, this is backend work: reading the request, turning it into `CloseReasonOptions`, and deciding what the person sees when it's refused. All of it is Go, and it can be tested by posting the form with no HTML at all. #54 would then only add the inputs and the display. This is the path from the close button to the service:

```
 browser: "Close" button on the issue page             ← #54: the dropdown / text box / number box
      │  POST …/comments   status=close  (+ close_reason, close_reason_text, close_duplicate_index)
      ▼
 services/forms/repo_form.go   CreateCommentForm       ← (A) new fields + a method that builds CloseReasonOptions
      ▼
 routers/web/repo/issue_comment.go   NewComment        ← (B) call CloseIssueWithReason; turn the 3 errors into messages
      ▼
 services/issue  CloseIssueWithReason                  done (commits 3–5)
```

### What it would change

**(A) The form.** Today `CreateCommentForm` only has `Status` ("close" or "reopen"). It would get three fields:
- the reason, sent as a name such as `not_planned`, not a number;
- the "other" text;
- the duplicate number.

A small method would turn those fields into `CloseReasonOptions`. Gitea already does exactly this for code review: `SubmitReviewForm.Type` arrives as `"approve"`, `"comment"` or `"reject"`, and its `ReviewType()` method maps the name to the integer enum, falling back to `ReviewTypeUnknown` for anything else. Names keep the storage numbers out of HTML and JavaScript, where Decision 3 said they must never be renumbered. An unknown name would map to an out-of-range value, and `Validate` already refuses those.

**(B) The handler.** `NewComment` currently calls `CloseIssue(ctx, issue, ctx.Doer, "")`. It would call `CloseIssueWithReason` with the options from (A).

There's one easy-to-miss problem there. Today, any close error other than "open dependencies" is only logged: the page redirects and the issue quietly stays open. That was harmless when closing couldn't fail for input reasons, but a bad reason would now fail silently. So the three new errors need a flash message, the way `ErrDependenciesLeft` already gets one. That means adding a user-visible string to the locale file, which is the only piece that touches presentation.

An empty form sends no reason, so it maps to "no reason", which stays valid. Until #54 adds the inputs, the button behaves exactly as it does now.

### What it would deliberately leave alone

- **Bulk close** on the issue list (`UpdateIssueStatus`) takes `action=close` and a list of IDs. One text or one duplicate target for many issues at once doesn't make sense, so it keeps calling the no-reason `CloseIssue`.
- **The API** (`routers/api/v1/repo/issue.go`) stays with #55, as the issue's Out of Scope section says.

### Size and tests

It's two small commits:
1. The form fields and mapping method, with unit tests: each name maps correctly, and unknown or empty names are handled.
2. The handler and the flash message, with an integration test that posts the comment form. One case closes with `not_planned` and checks it's stored. Another sends a bad reason and checks the issue stays open and a flash appears.

Want me to go ahead with those two, one at a time, as with the others?

```text
}

// NameMapper represents a form tag name mapper.
type NameMapper func(string) string

var nameMapper = func(field string) string {
	newstr := make([]rune, 0, len(field))
	for i, chr := range field {
		if isUpper := 'A' <= chr && chr <= 'Z'; isUpper {
			if i > 0 {
				newstr = append(newstr, '_')
			}
			chr -= ('A' - 'a')
		}
		newstr = append(newstr, chr)
	}
	return string(newstr)
}

// SetNameMapper sets name mapper.
func SetNameMapper(nm NameMapper) {
	nameMapper = nm
}
```

```text
1	# Issue #53 — design decisions
2	
3	### Decision 7: The duplicate target is given as its number in the repository, and stored as its ID
4	
5	**Decision:** A close as duplicate takes the number people see (`#12`, `DuplicateIndex`), looks it up with `GetIssueByIndex(repoID, number)` inside the close transaction, and stores the target's global ID on the issue and in the close comment's metadata. Any issue or pull request with that number in the same repository can be the target, open or closed; the issue itself and numbers that exist only in other repositories are rejected with `ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate`.
6	**Alternatives Considered:** Take the target's global ID, picked from a search dropdown, the way adding a dependency does (`routers/web/repo/issue_dependency.go`).
7	**Rationale:** Looking up by repository and number is how Gitea resolves every number a person gives (issue URLs, `fixes #12` in commits), and it keeps the target in the same repository without a separate check. The dependency form takes an ID, so it has to compare repositories itself. Storing the ID matches every other link between issues (`DependentIssueID`, `RefIssueID`), because a number only means something within one repository.
8	**Consequences:** Cross-repository duplicates are not possible, as AC4 intends. A search dropdown in #54 has to send the number, not the ID. Reading the target back takes a separate lookup by ID, and a deleted target shows up as "not found" rather than an error.
9	
10	### Decision 8: The issue page loads the duplicate target in this issue, not in #54
11	
12	**Decision:** `routers/web/repo/issue_view.go` calls `Comment.LoadCloseDuplicateIssue` for close comments, in the same place and the same way it loads the issue named by a dependency comment, and tolerates a deleted target.
13	**Alternatives Considered:** Add only the model loader in #53, and let #54 call it together with the template that shows it.
14	**Rationale:** AC4 says the close comment has the target issue loaded (number, title, link). Loading it where every other comment type's linked data is loaded makes that true within #53, and leaves #54 with template work only.
15	**Consequences:** Until #54 renders it, each close-as-duplicate comment costs one extra lookup when the issue page is viewed. Close comments without a duplicate return before any lookup.
```

```bash
### Decision 9: The web close form carries the reason in this issue; the UI inputs come in #54

**Decision:** The backend half of the web close path is done in #53. `CreateCommentForm` gains the reason fields, and `NewComment` in `routers/web/repo/issue_comment.go` calls `CloseIssueWithReason` and shows a flash message when the reason is refused. #54 only adds the inputs to the template and the display. Bulk close on the issue list (`UpdateIssueStatus`) keeps closing with no reason, and the API stays with #55.
**Alternatives Considered:** Leave the handler on `CloseIssue` and let #54 wire the form, the handler and the template together.
**Rationale:** Reading the request, building `CloseReasonOptions` and turning refusals into a response are server-side work that can be tested by posting the form, with no HTML involved. It also fixes a silent failure: the handler only logs close errors other than open dependencies, so a refused reason would otherwise leave the issue open with no message. Bulk close takes one action for many issues, where a single text or duplicate target doesn't make sense.
**Consequences:** Until #54 adds the inputs, the form sends no reason and the close button behaves exactly as before. Refusals need a user-visible string in the locale file. Bulk close cannot record a reason.

### Decision 10: The form sends the reason as a name, not its stored number

**Decision:** The close form sends `close_reason` as `completed`, `not_planned`, `duplicate` or `other`, and `CreateCommentForm.CloseReasonOptions()` maps the name to the `CloseReason` value. An empty name means no reason; an unknown name maps to `CloseReasonUnknown`, which `Validate` rejects.
**Alternatives Considered:** Send the stored integer (`close_reason=2`) and convert it directly.
**Rationale:** This is how the review form already works: `SubmitReviewForm.Type` arrives as `approve`, `comment` or `reject`, and `ReviewType()` maps it, falling back to `ReviewTypeUnknown`. The stored numbers are a storage detail that must never be renumbered (Decision 3), so they should not leak into HTML and JavaScript. `not_planned` matches the name GitHub's API uses.
**Consequences:** The names become part of the form contract that #54's template must send. #55's API can use the same names but will need its own mapping, as the review API does.
EOF
```

```text
+	CloseReasonText     string
+	CloseDuplicateIndex int64
+}
+
+// CloseReasonOptions maps the close reason fields; an empty name means no reason,
+// and an unknown one maps to CloseReasonUnknown so that Validate rejects it.
+func (f *CreateCommentForm) CloseReasonOptions() issues_model.CloseReasonOptions {
+	opts := issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Text: f.CloseReasonText, DuplicateIndex: f.CloseDuplicateIndex}
+	switch f.CloseReason {
+	case "":
+		opts.Reason = issues_model.CloseReasonNone
+	case "completed":
+		opts.Reason = issues_model.CloseReasonCompleted
+	case "not_planned":
+		opts.Reason = issues_model.CloseReasonNotPlanned
+	case "duplicate":
+		opts.Reason = issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate
+	case "other":
+		opts.Reason = issues_model.CloseReasonOther
+	default:
+		opts.Reason = issues_model.CloseReasonUnknown
+	}
+	return opts
 }
```

**The changes:**
- **`services/forms/repo_form.go`:** `CreateCommentForm` gets `CloseReason`, `CloseReasonText` and `CloseDuplicateIndex`. They bind to `close_reason`, `close_reason_text` and `close_duplicate_index` without tags, because Gitea converts field names to snake case (`modules/web/middleware/binding.go`, confirmed with Gitea's own `util.ToSnakeCase`). The `CloseReasonOptions()` method is shaped like `SubmitReviewForm.ReviewType()`: it maps each name to its value, an empty name to "no reason", and anything else to "unknown".
- **`models/issues/issue_close_reason.go`:** `CloseReasonUnknown = -1`, modelled on `ReviewTypeUnknown = -1`. It's never stored, because `Validate` rejects it.
- **`services/forms/repo_form_test.go`:** each name maps correctly. `"2"` (the stored number) and `"Completed"` (wrong case) are unknown. Text and number pass through, and an unknown name ends up refused by `Validate`. I broke the method two ways (no fallback for unknown names; `not_planned` mapped wrong) and the test caught both.

```text
04fa76c1d8 feat(issues): accept close reason fields on the comment form
## Conventions & invariants

- **Only ever edit `locale_en-US.json`.** Every other locale file is written by Crowdin
  (`crowdin.yml` sets `en-US` as the source). Editing one by hand is overwritten on the next sync,
  and a PR that touches other locale files will be asked to revert them.
- Keys are dotted and grouped by area (`repo.issues.new`, `settings.`, `admin.`). Put a new key
  next to its neighbours rather than at the end.
- Templates use `{{ctx.Locale.Tr "key"}}`, or `TrN` for plurals. TypeScript uses `trN` from
  `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts`; strings reach the frontend through `window.config.i18n`
  (`templates/base/head_script.tmpl`), which is deliberately limited to general text — anything
  specialised should arrive via an API response, a `data-` attribute, or `pageData`.
- A plural is **two keys** suffixed `_1` and `_n`, both interpolating `%d` — see
  `actions.runs.graph_jobs_count_1` and `_n`. `TrN` and `trN` pick the form from the count.
- The `data-` attribute carrying a string to TypeScript is named `data-locale-<name>`, read with
  `getAttribute` — `templates/repo/actions/view_component.tmpl` passes both plural forms this way.
- **Never write a user-visible literal** in a template, a handler, or a `.ts` file.
- Errors whose message reaches the user go through `util.ErrorWrapTranslatable`
  (`modules-util-and-generics.md`), not a plain `fmt.Errorf`.
- `crowdin.yml` sets `skip_untranslated_strings` and `export_only_approved`, so a missing
  translation falls back rather than shipping an empty string.

## Recipes
## Gotchas

- A missing key renders as the key itself — visible in the UI but easy to miss on a rarely-hit
  branch.
- Changing an existing key's *text* is fine; changing the *key name* invalidates every existing
  translation for it.
- `options/locale` is embedded into the binary (`modules/options`), so a locale change needs a
  rebuild to appear.

## Related
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-27 22:10:22Z)**_

Commit 6b is ready for you to commit: three files. The web close button now passes the form's reason through, and every refusal tells the person why.

### Why locale strings

Yes, that's the reason. When `NewComment` gets a refusal back from the model, the backend has to tell the person *why*, the same way it already does for the other close refusal:

- **Today there's exactly one close refusal with a message:** open dependencies. For it, the handler shows `ctx.Tr("repo.issues.dependency.issue_close_blocked")` as a flash message. Our three errors are handled in the same `if … else if` chain, the same way.
- **Without a message, the refusal would be silent.** The handler only logs other errors, so the page would redirect and the issue would quietly stay open.
- **Gitea never puts user-visible text in Go code.** The i18n doc says so outright: "never write a user-visible literal in a template, a handler, or a `.ts` file". The handler therefore can't write the English sentence itself. It names a key, and `ctx.Tr` looks up the text in the person's language, falling back to `locale_en-US.json`, the only file we edit.
- **The errors' own `Error()` text isn't suitable either.** Messages like `invalid duplicate target: … [index: 9999]` are for the log, not for people.

The server produces the message and shows it on the page it redirects to, so no template or JavaScript changes are needed. That's why it belongs in #53, not #54.

I used **three keys, one per error**, not the single one I first mentioned, so each message says what to fix. The text message gets the 255 from `CloseReasonTextMaxLength` through `%d`, so the number isn't written in two places.

### What changed

- **`routers/web/repo/issue_comment.go`:** `NewComment` calls `CloseIssueWithReason(…, form.CloseReasonOptions())`. Three `else if` branches after the dependency branch show the matching flash, and the log line now names the function actually called.
- **`options/locale/locale_en-US.json`:** `repo.issues.close_reason.not_allowed`, `.text_invalid` and `.duplicate_invalid`, placed next to the close button's strings so #54 can add its labels to the same group.
- **`tests/integration/issue_test.go`:** `TestIssueCommentCloseWithReason` posts the real form. It checks `not_planned`, "other" with text and duplicate #1 are stored, which proves all three form keys bind. It also checks two refusals leave the issue open with the exact flash text, which would catch a missing key rendering as its name.

### Checks

- **The new integration test** runs in 0.44s. I broke it three ways (handler back on `CloseIssue`, the flash for text errors removed, a locale key deleted) and each break failed it.
- **`TestIssueCommentClose` still passes,** so the close button without a reason is unchanged.
- **Lint, suites, formatting:** the Go lint, the `routers/web/repo` and `services/forms` suites, `make fmt`, whitespace and `make lint-editorconfig` are clean. The locale file passes the JSON lint when linted on its own. `make lint-json` as a whole fails on `data/indexers/…/index_meta.json`, a file your local Gitea wrote into the ignored `/data` directory, which has nothing to do with this change.

```
git add routers/web/repo/issue_comment.go options/locale/locale_en-US.json tests/integration/issue_test.go
```

```markdown
# Issue #53 — design decisions

## Acceptance criteria → tests

Files:
- `v343_test.go` is `models/migrations/v1_27/v343_test.go`.
- `close_reason_test.go` is `models/issues/issue_close_reason_test.go`.
- `repo_form_test.go` is `services/forms/repo_form_test.go`.
- `issue_test.go` is `tests/integration/issue_test.go`.

| AC | Tests | What they check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC1: migration adds the columns; existing rows have no reason | `Test_AddCloseReasonToIssue` (`v343_test.go`) | Migration 343 runs on an open issue, a closed issue, an open PR and a closed PR; all four read back with no reason, no text, no target |
| | `TestIssueCloseReasonPersists` (`close_reason_test.go`) | A fresh-install schema (built from the live model) gives existing rows the defaults, and all three columns save and load |
| | `TestCloseIssueRecordsReason/no_reason` (`close_reason_test.go`) | A close comment with no metadata, like every comment from before the migration, reads as no reason through `MetaCloseReason()` |
| AC2: a valid reason is stored on the issue and its close comment | `TestCloseIssueRecordsReason` (`close_reason_test.go`) | Completed, other with text, and not planned: stored on the issue row and, after a reload, in the close comment's metadata |
| | `TestCloseIssueAsDuplicate` (`close_reason_test.go`) | Duplicate: reason and target stored on the issue row and in the close comment |
| | `TestIssueCommentCloseWithReason/not_planned`, `/other_with_text`, `/duplicate` (`issue_test.go`) | The same through the real web close form, which also proves the three form keys bind |
| AC3: "other" text that is empty or over 255 characters is rejected, and the issue stays open; valid text is stored | `TestCloseReasonOptionsValidate` (`close_reason_test.go`) | No text, whitespace-only text and 256 characters are rejected with `ErrInvalidCloseReasonText`; 255 two-byte characters pass (characters are counted, not bytes); text with another reason is rejected |
| | `TestCloseIssueInvalidReasonLeavesItOpen/other_with_no_text` (`close_reason_test.go`) | The issue stays open in the database and in memory, and no close comment is created |
| | `TestCloseIssueRecordsReason/other_with_text`, `/whitespace-only_text_is_not_stored` (`close_reason_test.go`) | Valid text is stored; text sent with another reason is not |
| | `TestIssueCommentCloseWithReason/refused_reason_leaves_the_issue_open` (`issue_test.go`) | Through the web form: the issue stays open and the text-error flash message is shown |
| AC4: a duplicate target that is missing, the issue itself, or not in this repository is rejected; a valid target is stored and loaded | `TestCloseReasonOptionsValidate` (`close_reason_test.go`) | Duplicate with no number or a negative one, and a number with another reason or none, are rejected with `ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate` |
| | `TestCloseIssueInvalidReasonLeavesItOpen/duplicate_of_itself`, `/duplicate_of_a_number_that_does_not_exist`, `/duplicate_of_a_number_only_in_another_repository` (`close_reason_test.go`) | Each is rejected and the issue stays open, with no close comment |
| | `TestCloseIssueAsDuplicate` (`close_reason_test.go`) | The target is stored as its global ID; `LoadCloseDuplicateIssue` gives its number, title and link (including the repository) |
| | `TestLoadCloseDuplicateIssueDeletedTarget` (`close_reason_test.go`) | A deleted target returns "not found", which the issue page tolerates |
| | `TestIssueCommentCloseWithReason/duplicate`, `/refused_reason_leaves_the_issue_open` (`issue_test.go`) | Through the web form: #1 is stored as the target, and #9999 is refused with the duplicate flash message |
| AC5: a PR cannot be closed as completed; the allowed lists differ | `TestAllowedCloseReasons` (`close_reason_test.go`) | The issue list has all four reasons; the PR list leaves out completed |
| | `TestCloseReasonOptionsValidate/completed_pull_request`, `/out_of_range` (`close_reason_test.go`) | Rejected with `ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed` |
| | `TestCloseIssueInvalidReasonLeavesItOpen/pull_request_closed_as_completed` (`close_reason_test.go`) | The PR stays open, with no close comment |
| | `TestCreateCommentForm_CloseReasonOptions` (`repo_form_test.go`) | The form maps names to reasons; an unknown name (including the stored number `2`) is rejected with the same error |
| AC6: reopening clears the issue's reason; the earlier close comment keeps its own | `TestReopenIssueClearsReason` (`close_reason_test.go`) | For "other" with text and for duplicate: after reopening, the issue has no reason, text or target; the old close comment still has its reason, text and a loadable target; the reopen comment has no metadata |
| AC7: existing close paths still work, with no reason; a merge records none | `TestCloseIssueRecordsReason/no_reason`, `TestCloseReasonOptionsValidate/no_reason*` (`close_reason_test.go`) | Closing with no reason succeeds and stores none |
| | `TestIssueCommentClose` (`issue_test.go`, existing) | The web close button with no reason still closes, and the issue page still renders |
| | `TestAPIIssue` (`tests/integration/api_issue_test.go`, existing) | Closing through the API still works |
| | `TestPullMerge` (`tests/integration/pull_merge_test.go`, existing) | Merging a PR still works; it closes through `SetIssueAsClosed` with an empty reason |
| | `TestUpdateIssuesCommit*` (`services/issue/commit_test.go`, existing) | Commit keywords still close issues |
| | `TestPullBranchDelete` (`tests/integration/pull_create_test.go`, existing) | Deleting a PR's branch, which closes the PR, still works |
| | existing `models/issues` tests `dependency_test.go`, `issue_xref_test.go` | Still pass when closing with an empty reason |

### Not covered, or only partly

- **AC3, "stored exactly as entered":** the stored text in the tests has no leading or trailing spaces, so nothing shows that the text is stored untrimmed.
- **AC3, over 255 characters through the close path:** rejected by `Validate`, but only the empty-text case is run through a full close. Any `Validate` error returns before anything is written, so the result would be the same.
- **AC4, the issue page with a real duplicate:** the loader is tested in the model, and the page is rendered in a test only with close comments that have no duplicate. No test views a page with a close-as-duplicate comment.
- **AC7:**
  - Bulk close on the issue list (`UpdateIssueStatus`) has no test.
  - `TestPullBranchDelete` runs the branch-deletion close but checks only that the page loads.
  - `TestPullMerge` doesn't check that the merged PR has no reason.

```

**Recommendation: leave both as they are for #53. List them in the PR's test strategy, and open an issue only for bulk close, if the team wants it.**

- **Bulk close.** #53 never touched `UpdateIssueStatus`: it still calls `CloseIssue`, which is now the no-reason wrapper, and that wrapper is covered by the no-reason tests. The missing test already existed before this work, since nothing in `tests/integration` posts to the bulk status endpoint. It becomes a real gap only if someone later gives bulk close a reason, and that issue should bring its own test. If your team wants small test-coverage issues, "test: integration test for bulk close and reopen" would make a clean one, but it doesn't block #53.
- **Branch deletion.** Adding the check is technically small, a few assertions in `TestPullBranchDelete`. Two things argue against it here, though. It means editing an upstream test for a path #53 didn't change, and upstream test files are where future merges from Gitea will conflict. The payoff is also low, because that path goes through the same unchanged wrapper. I'd let it be, and not open an issue for it.

The course's PR format asks you to name what isn't tested automatically, so both belong in the PR's test strategy section.

```text
func SetMerged(ctx context.Context, pr *issues_model.PullRequest, mergedCommitID string, mergedTimeStamp timeutil.TimeStamp, merger *user_model.User, mergeStatus issues_model.PullRequestStatus) (bool, error) {
	if pr.HasMerged {
		return false, fmt.Errorf("PullRequest[%d] already merged", pr.Index)
	}

	pr.HasMerged = true
	pr.MergedCommitID = mergedCommitID
	pr.MergedUnix = mergedTimeStamp
	pr.Merger = merger
	pr.MergerID = merger.ID
	pr.Status = mergeStatus
	// reset the conflicted files as there cannot be any if we're merged
	pr.ConflictedFiles = []string{}

	if pr.MergedCommitID == "" || pr.MergedUnix == 0 || pr.Merger == nil {
		return false, fmt.Errorf("unable to merge PullRequest[%d], some required fields are empty", pr.Index)
	}

	return db.WithTx2(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) (bool, error) {
```

```text
## Conventions & invariants

**Forms**

- A form is a plain struct with `binding:"..."` tags: `binding:"Required;MaxSize(255)"`. Field
  names map from the request automatically; add `form:"assignee_ids"` only when the request field
  name differs from the Go field name.
- A form that needs the standard error handling implements
  `Validate(req *http.Request, errs binding.Errors) binding.Errors` and returns
  `middleware.Validate(errs, ctx.Data, f, ctx.Locale)` — copy the body from a neighbouring form
  verbatim; it is boilerplate, not a decision.
- Validation messages are locale keys, resolved through `ctx.Locale` by `middleware.Validate`.
  `validation.AddBindingRules` is called once from `registerWebRoutes` and registers the custom
  rules; a new rule goes there, not into the form.
- The route wires the form with `web.Bind(forms.XxxForm{})` and the handler reads it back with
  `web.GetForm(ctx)`, type-asserted to the form type.

**Converters**

- Naming is `To<Thing>` for the plain conversion and `To<Thing>List` for a slice. Where both an
  internal and an API-facing variant exist, the API one is `ToAPI<Thing>`.
- A converter whose output depends on permissions or needs more queries takes
  `(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, model *T)` — `ToAPIIssue` is the pattern. Pass the
  real doer, never `nil`, unless the neighbouring call sites do. A pure value conversion takes just
  the model (`ToEmail`, `ToTag`).
- Converters return `modules/structs` types. They must not query for anything a caller could have
  loaded; a converter that fans out queries per item turns a list endpoint into an N+1.

## Recipes

**Add a field to a form.** Add the struct field with its `binding` tag, add the locale key for any
new validation message to `options/locale/locale_en-US.json`, then read it in the handler from
`web.GetForm(ctx)`. Existing forms have tests in `services/forms/repo_form_test.go` — extend them
rather than adding an integration test.

**Expose a new model field over the API.** Add the field to the `modules/structs` type, set it in
the matching `services/convert` function, and check whether the swagger response registration in
`routers/api/v1/swagger/` already covers the struct (it usually does). Then
`make generate-swagger`.

## Gotchas
=== routers-web.md conventions+recipes ===
## Conventions & invariants

- A handler is `func Foo(ctx *context.Context)` from `gitea.dev/services/context`. It puts data in
  `ctx.Data`, then calls `ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplFoo)`.
- Not every handler renders a template: one backing a JS-driven widget on an otherwise-HTML page
  calls `ctx.JSON` instead, e.g. `routers/web/repo/issue_suggestions.go`. That stays in
  `routers/web`, distinct from the `/api/v1` JSON layer (`routers-api-v1.md`).
- `tplFoo` is a package-level `templates.TplName` constant whose value is a path under `templates/`
  without the extension — `tplIssues templates.TplName = "repo/issue/list"`.
- `ctx.Data` is the only channel from handler to template. A template cannot reach anything the
  handler did not put there.
- Sign-in guards are local variables built at the top of `registerWebRoutes` from
  `verifyAuthWithOptions`: `reqSignIn`, `reqSignOut`, `optSignIn`, `optExploreSignIn`. A new guard
  is declared there too, not in a subpackage.
- Repo pages get `context.RepoAssignment` (see `services-context.md`), which fills `ctx.Repo`;
  ref-scoped pages add `context.RepoRefByType`.
- A POST that takes a form is registered as
  `m.Post("/path", web.Bind(forms.XxxForm{}), handler)`; the handler reads it back with
  `web.GetForm(ctx)`.
- The middleware chain in `Routes` is, in order: `chi_middleware.GetHead`, optional gzip,
  `common.MustInitSessioner`, `context.Contexter`, the web auth middleware, `goGet`,
  `common.PageGlobalData`, then `common.BlockExpensive` and `common.QoS`.

## Recipes

**Add a page.**

1. Handler in the matching `routers/web/<area>/` file, signature `func(ctx *context.Context)`.
2. A `templates.TplName` constant beside the other constants in that file.
3. The template file at the matching path under `templates/`.
4. The route inside the right `m.Group` in `registerWebRoutes`, with the guards that group needs.
5. Any user-visible string as a key in `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` — never a literal.

**Add a form POST.** Do the above, plus a form struct in `services/forms/` and `web.Bind` on the
route. See `services-forms-and-convert.md`.

**Find the template behind a page you are looking at.** Outside production, `ctx.HTML` sets
`ctx.Data["TemplateName"]` and `templates/base/footer_content.tmpl` prints it in the page footer, so
a dev instance names its own template on every page. Failing that, grep the visible string in
`options/locale/locale_en-US.json` for its key, then grep that key under `templates/`. To go the
other way, from a template to its handler, grep for the `TplName` value — the template path without
the extension.

## Gotchas

- The static routes registered on `routes` *before* the `mid` slice is assembled (`/assets/*`,
  `/avatars/*`, `/favicon.ico`, `/api/healthz`) deliberately bypass session and auth middleware.
  Do not add an authenticated route there.
- `registerWebRoutes` is long. Find your group by URL prefix rather than reading top to bottom, and
  add the route to the group that already carries the guards you need instead of re-listing them.
- `ctx.HTML` after something has already written the response is a bug; `ctx.Written()` reports
  whether that happened.
```
