# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

  ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (AC1 as amended):
  - AC1: Given a database with existing open and closed issues and PRs, when the migration runs, then the close-reason columns exist on the `issue` table and every existing issue and PR has an empty reason; existing close comments, which have no close-reason metadata, also read as having no reason.

  - AC4: Given the reason "duplicate", when the target number does not exist in the same repository or is the issue itself, then the close is rejected with its own error; a valid target is stored, and the close comment has the target issue loaded (number, title, link).

  - AC6: Given an issue closed with a reason, when it is reopened, then the issue's reason is cleared and the earlier close comment keeps its reason.
  - AC7: Given any existing close path (web, bulk, commit keyword, merged PR, branch deletion, API), when it closes an issue without a reason, then the close succeeds as before with an empty reason, and merging a PR still records no reason.
  
  DESIGN DECISIONS:
  1. services/issue CloseIssue is kept as a backwards-compatibility wrapper that calls the new CloseIssueWithReason with an empty reason; callers that should supply a reason are changed.
  2. Whitespace-only "other" text counts as empty (trimmed before the empty check).
  3. The issue table gets close_reason (Go type CloseReason int, SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, 0 = none), close_reason_text (VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL DEFAULT '', only for "other") and close_duplicate_issue_id (NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, the target's global issue ID). No database ENUM; values must never be renumbered.
  4. Close comments store reason, text and duplicate target in the existing Comment.CommentMetaData JSON field (written once, never updated), not new comment columns; migration only touches `issue`.
  5. Text sent with any reason other than "other" is rejected (ErrInvalidCloseReasonText); whitespace-only text counts as no text; stored text is empty unless the reason is "other".
  6. Validation happens in models/issues SetIssueAsClosed inside the close transaction (the merge path in services/pull/merge.go SetMerged calls SetIssueAsClosed directly).
  7. The duplicate target is given as the per-repository number (CloseReasonOptions.DuplicateIndex), resolved with GetIssueByIndex(issue.RepoID, n) inside the transaction, stored as the target's global ID on the issue and in the comment metadata; any issue or PR in the same repo, open or closed; self and other-repo numbers rejected with ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate.
  8. routers/web/repo/issue_view.go loads the duplicate target for close comments (Comment.LoadCloseDuplicateIssue, which also loads the target's repo so Link works), tolerating a deleted target (ErrIssueNotExist).
  9. Bulk close (UpdateIssueStatus) keeps closing with no reason; the API stays with #55.
  10. The form sends close_reason as a name (completed, not_planned, duplicate, other); CreateCommentForm.CloseReasonOptions() maps it; empty = none; unknown = CloseReasonUnknown (-1), which Validate rejects.

  CONTEXT — Gitea fork (CSCI 435 course), repo at /home/mantmant/Documents/CSCI435/gitea, branch feat/issue-53-issue-reason-backend, 11 commits ahead of main (main == origin/main). Review with: git diff main..HEAD (34 files).
  
  ISSUE #53: backend to store and retrieve the reason an issue or PR was closed. UI display is issue #54, API access is issue #55 (both out of scope).
  
  ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (AC1 as amended):
  - AC1: Given a database with existing open and closed issues and PRs, when the migration runs, then the close-reason columns exist on the `issue` table and every existing issue and PR has an empty reason; existing close comments, which have no close-reason metadata, also read as having no reason.
  - AC2: Given an open issue, when it is closed through the close service with a valid reason (completed, not planned, duplicate or other), then both the issue and its new close timeline comment store that reason.
  - AC3: Given the reason "other", when the text is empty or longer than 255 characters, then the close is rejected with its own error and the issue stays open; valid text is stored exactly as entered.
  - AC4: Given the reason "duplicate", when the target number does not exist in the same repository or is the issue itself, then the close is rejected with its own error; a valid target is stored, and the close comment has the target issue loaded (number, title, link).
  - AC5: Given a pull request, when it is closed as "completed", then the close is rejected with its own error; the allowed-reasons list for a PR leaves out "completed" and an issue's list includes all four.
  - AC6: Given an issue closed with a reason, when it is reopened, then the issue's reason is cleared and the earlier close comment keeps its reason.
  - AC7: Given any existing close path (web, bulk, commit keyword, merged PR, branch deletion, API), when it closes an issue without a reason, then the close succeeds as before with an empty reason, and merging a PR still records no reason.
  
  DESIGN DECISIONS:
  1. services/issue CloseIssue is kept as a backwards-compatibility wrapper that calls the new CloseIssueWithReason with an empty reason; callers that should supply a reason are changed.
  2. Whitespace-only "other" text counts as empty (trimmed before the empty check).
  3. The issue table gets close_reason (Go type CloseReason int, SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, 0 = none), close_reason_text (VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL DEFAULT '', only for "other") and close_duplicate_issue_id (NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, the target's global issue ID). No database ENUM; values must never be renumbered.
  4. Close comments store reason, text and duplicate target in the existing Comment.CommentMetaData JSON field (written once, never updated), not new comment columns; migration only touches `issue`.
  5. Text sent with any reason other than "other" is rejected (ErrInvalidCloseReasonText); whitespace-only text counts as no text; stored text is empty unless the reason is "other".
  6. Validation happens in models/issues SetIssueAsClosed inside the close transaction (the merge path in services/pull/merge.go SetMerged calls SetIssueAsClosed directly).
  7. The duplicate target is given as the per-repository number (CloseReasonOptions.DuplicateIndex), resolved with GetIssueByIndex(issue.RepoID, n) inside the transaction, stored as the target's global ID on the issue and in the comment metadata; any issue or PR in the same repo, open or closed; self and other-repo numbers rejected with ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate.
  8. routers/web/repo/issue_view.go loads the duplicate target for close comments (Comment.LoadCloseDuplicateIssue, which also loads the target's repo so Link works), tolerating a deleted target (ErrIssueNotExist).
  9. The web close form handler NewComment (routers/web/repo/issue_comment.go) calls CloseIssueWithReason with the form's options and maps the three refusals to flash messages (three new keys repo.issues.close_reason.* in options/locale/locale_en-US.json). Bulk close (UpdateIssueStatus) keeps closing with no reason; the API stays with #55.
  10. The form sends close_reason as a name (completed, not_planned, duplicate, other); CreateCommentForm.CloseReasonOptions() maps it; empty = none; unknown = CloseReasonUnknown (-1), which Validate rejects.
  Other: reopening (setIssueAsReopen) clears the issue's three reason fields; comment metadata is untouched. Known accepted limitation: on MSSQL, NVARCHAR counts UTF-16 units, so over ~127 astral-plane characters pass the 255-character check but overflow on MSSQL only.
  
  AC → TEST MAPPING (claimed):
  - AC1: Test_AddCloseReasonToIssue (models/migrations/v1_27/v343_test.go); TestIssueCloseReasonPersists; TestCloseIssueRecordsReason/no_reason (models/issues/issue_close_reason_test.go).
  - AC2: TestCloseIssueRecordsReason (completed, other with text, not planned); TestCloseIssueAsDuplicate; TestIssueCommentCloseWithReason/not_planned, /other_with_text, /duplicate (tests/integration/issue_test.go).
  - AC3: TestCloseReasonOptionsValidate; TestCloseIssueInvalidReasonLeavesItOpen/other_with_no_text; TestCloseIssueRecordsReason/other_with_text, /other_text_is_stored_as_entered, /whitespace-only_text_is_not_stored; TestIssueCommentCloseWithReason/refused_reason_leaves_the_issue_open.
  - AC4: TestCloseReasonOptionsValidate (duplicate cases); TestCloseIssueInvalidReasonLeavesItOpen/duplicate_of_itself, /duplicate_of_a_number_that_does_not_exist, /duplicate_of_a_number_only_in_another_repository; TestCloseIssueAsDuplicate; TestLoadCloseDuplicateIssueDeletedTarget; TestIssueCommentCloseWithReason/duplicate (also loads the issue page), /refused_reason_leaves_the_issue_open.
  - AC5: TestAllowedCloseReasons; TestCloseReasonOptionsValidate/completed_pull_request, /out_of_range; TestCloseIssueInvalidReasonLeavesItOpen/pull_request_closed_as_completed; TestCreateCommentForm_CloseReasonOptions (services/forms/repo_form_test.go).
  - AC6: TestReopenIssueClearsReason.
  - AC7: TestCloseIssueRecordsReason/no_reason; TestCloseReasonOptionsValidate/no_reason*; TestSetMergedRecordsNoCloseReason (services/pull/merge_test.go); existing TestIssueCommentClose, TestAPIIssue, TestPullMerge, TestUpdateIssuesCommit* (services/issue/commit_test.go), TestPullBranchDelete; existing dependency_test.go and issue_xref_test.go.
  - Declared not covered: AC3 over-255 only via Validate (not a full close); bulk close has no test (pre-existing, code unchanged); TestPullBranchDelete only checks the page loads.

Do not run builds, tests, linters, make targets, go vet, or anything that writes to the tree or shared test directories (another agent is running tests concurrently). Do not flag the absence of UI (issue #54) or API (issue #55) work as a defect, but do flag if the backend contract would make #54/#55 hard or wrong. Also list, under "checked", the specific things you verified and found correct.
  
  Dimension: data integrity, transactions and databases. Check: transaction boundaries (validation and the duplicate lookup inside db.WithTx; notify_service calls stay outside the transaction); the in-memory issue struct is not mutated when a close is refused or fails; ErrIssueAlreadyChanged/concurrent close/reopen races with the new columns; xorm Cols() lists include every new column where needed and nowhere they should not be; migration 343 correctness on SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL and MSSQL (SMALLINT, VARCHAR(255) → NVARCHAR on MSSQL via DEFAULT_VARCHAR, NOT NULL DEFAULT, SyncWithOptions with IgnoreDropIndices/IgnoreConstrains, local struct named Issue maps to table issue); fresh-install schema (the live Issue model tags) matches the upgraded schema (the migration's local struct) exactly; CommentMetaData JSON: omitempty behaviour, unmarshalling old rows without the new keys, the CloseReason int type in JSON; CloseReasonUnknown (-1) can never be stored; the known MSSQL limitation (NVARCHAR counts UTF-16 units, so >127 astral characters pass validation but overflow on MSSQL) — confirm or refute it and whether anything else is affected.

  - AC1: Given a database with existing open and closed issues and PRs, when the migration runs, then the close-reason columns exist on the `issue` table and every existing issue and PR has an empty reason; existing close comments, which have no close-reason metadata, also read as having no reason.
  - AC2: Given an open issue, when it is closed through the close service with a valid reason (completed, not planned, duplicate or other), then both the issue and its new close timeline comment store that reason.
  - AC3: Given the reason "other", when the text is empty or longer than 255 characters, then the close is rejected with its own error and the issue stays open; valid text is stored exactly as entered.
  - AC4: Given the reason "duplicate", when the target number does not exist in the same repository or is the issue itself, then the close is rejected with its own error; a valid target is stored, and the close comment has the target issue loaded (number, title, link).
  - AC5: Given a pull request, when it is closed as "completed", then the close is rejected with its own error; the allowed-reasons list for a PR leaves out "completed" and an issue's list includes all four.
  - AC6: Given an issue closed with a reason, when it is reopened, then the issue's reason is cleared and the earlier close comment keeps its reason.
  - AC7: Given any existing close path (web, bulk, commit keyword, merged PR, branch deletion, API), when it closes an issue without a reason, then the close succeeds as before with an empty reason, and merging a PR still records no reason.
  
  DESIGN DECISIONS:
  1. services/issue CloseIssue is kept as a backwards-compatibility wrapper that calls the new CloseIssueWithReason with an empty reason; callers that should supply a reason are changed.
  2. Whitespace-only "other" text counts as empty (trimmed before the empty check).
  3. The issue table gets close_reason (Go type CloseReason int, SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, 0 = none), close_reason_text (VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL DEFAULT '', only for "other") and close_duplicate_issue_id (NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, the target's global issue ID). No database ENUM; values must never be renumbered.
  4. Close comments store reason, text and duplicate target in the existing Comment.CommentMetaData JSON field (written once, never updated), not new comment columns; migration only touches `issue`.
  5. Text sent with any reason other than "other" is rejected (ErrInvalidCloseReasonText); whitespace-only text counts as no text; stored text is empty unless the reason is "other".
  6. Validation happens in models/issues SetIssueAsClosed inside the close transaction (the merge path in services/pull/merge.go SetMerged calls SetIssueAsClosed directly).
  7. The duplicate target is given as the per-repository number (CloseReasonOptions.DuplicateIndex), resolved with GetIssueByIndex(issue.RepoID, n) inside the transaction, stored as the target's global ID on the issue and in the comment metadata; any issue or PR in the same repo, open or closed; self and other-repo numbers rejected with ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate.
  8. routers/web/repo/issue_view.go loads the duplicate target for close comments (Comment.LoadCloseDuplicateIssue, which also loads the target's repo so Link works), tolerating a deleted target (ErrIssueNotExist).
  9. The web close form handler NewComment (routers/web/repo/issue_comment.go) calls CloseIssueWithReason with the form's options and maps the three refusals to flash messages (three new keys repo.issues.close_reason.* in options/locale/locale_en-US.json). Bulk close (UpdateIssueStatus) keeps closing with no reason; the API stays with #55.
  10. The form sends close_reason as a name (completed, not_planned, duplicate, other); CreateCommentForm.CloseReasonOptions() maps it; empty = none; unknown = CloseReasonUnknown (-1), which Validate rejects.
  Other: reopening (setIssueAsReopen) clears the issue's three reason fields; comment metadata is untouched. Known accepted limitation: on MSSQL, NVARCHAR counts UTF-16 units, so over ~127 astral-plane characters pass the 255-character check but overflow on MSSQL only.
  
  AC → TEST MAPPING (claimed):
  - AC1: Test_AddCloseReasonToIssue (models/migrations/v1_27/v343_test.go); TestIssueCloseReasonPersists; TestCloseIssueRecordsReason/no_reason (models/issues/issue_close_reason_test.go).
  - AC2: TestCloseIssueRecordsReason (completed, other with text, not planned); TestCloseIssueAsDuplicate; TestIssueCommentCloseWithReason/not_planned, /other_with_text, /duplicate (tests/integration/issue_test.go).
  - AC3: TestCloseReasonOptionsValidate; TestCloseIssueInvalidReasonLeavesItOpen/other_with_no_text; TestCloseIssueRecordsReason/other_with_text, /other_text_is_stored_as_entered, /whitespace-only_text_is_not_stored; TestIssueCommentCloseWithReason/refused_reason_leaves_the_issue_open.
  - AC4: TestCloseReasonOptionsValidate (duplicate cases); TestCloseIssueInvalidReasonLeavesItOpen/duplicate_of_itself, /duplicate_of_a_number_that_does_not_exist, /duplicate_of_a_number_only_in_another_repository; TestCloseIssueAsDuplicate; TestLoadCloseDuplicateIssueDeletedTarget; TestIssueCommentCloseWithReason/duplicate (also loads the issue page), /refused_reason_leaves_the_issue_open.
  - AC5: TestAllowedCloseReasons; TestCloseReasonOptionsValidate/completed_pull_request, /out_of_range; TestCloseIssueInvalidReasonLeavesItOpen/pull_request_closed_as_completed; TestCreateCommentForm_CloseReasonOptions (services/forms/repo_form_test.go).
  - AC6: TestReopenIssueClearsReason.
  - AC7: TestCloseIssueRecordsReason/no_reason; TestCloseReasonOptionsValidate/no_reason*; TestSetMergedRecordsNoCloseReason (services/pull/merge_test.go); existing TestIssueCommentClose, TestAPIIssue, TestPullMerge, TestUpdateIssuesCommit* (services/issue/commit_test.go), TestPullBranchDelete; existing dependency_test.go and issue_xref_test.go.
  - Declared not covered: AC3 over-255 only via Validate (not a full close); bulk close has no test (pre-existing, code unchanged); TestPullBranchDelete only checks the page loads.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-27 22:31:08Z)**_

The verification workflow is running in the background. You can watch it with `/workflows`.

It's doing three things:
1. **Seven read-only reviewers** each check one dimension of the 34-file diff: AC1–AC4 correctness, AC5–AC7 and regressions, data and databases, web and security, conventions, tests, and docs. They're forbidden from running anything or changing the tree.
2. **One runner** executes the full suite, sequentially:
   - build, `gofmt`, `go vet` and the scoped lint;
   - the unit suites for every touched package, and all non-migration model packages;
   - `make migrations.individual.test`;
   - the five close-path integration tests, plus a wider sweep over the `TestIssue*`, `TestAPIIssue*`, `TestAPIEditIssue*` and merge tests;
   - `check.sh`, the locale lint and editorconfig;
   - whitespace across the whole branch diff, copyright headers on new files, and a clean-tree check before and after.
3. **Two skeptics per finding** try to refute it, one checking whether the claim is true in the code and one whether it actually matters given the ACs and decisions. A completeness critic then looks for anything nobody checked.

I'll report back when it finishes, with results split into confirmed, disputed and refuted. I won't change anything until you've seen the findings.

+func (c *Comment) MetaCloseReason() CloseReasonOptions {
+	if c.CommentMetaData == nil {
+		return CloseReasonOptions{}
+	}
+	return CloseReasonOptions{Reason: c.CommentMetaData.CloseReason, Text: c.CommentMetaData.CloseReasonText}
+}
+
+// LoadCloseDuplicateIssue loads the issue a close comment names as the duplicate target,
+// with its repository so that Link works. A deleted target returns ErrIssueNotExist.

116	@@ -0,0 +1,139 @@
117	+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
118	+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
119	+
120	+package issues
121	+
122	+import (
123	+	"fmt"
124	+	"slices"
125	+	"strings"
126	+	"unicode/utf8"
127	+
128	+	"gitea.dev/modules/util"
129	+)
130	+
131	+// CloseReason records why an issue or pull request was closed.
132	+// It is stored as an integer, so existing values must never be renumbered.
133	+type CloseReason int
134	+
135	+const (
136	+	CloseReasonNone       CloseReason = iota // 0
137	+	CloseReasonCompleted                     // 1
138	+	CloseReasonNotPlanned                    // 2
139	+	CloseReasonDuplicate                     // 3
140	+	CloseReasonOther                         // 4
141	+)
142	+
143	+// CloseReasonUnknown is never stored: it stands for an unrecognised reason name, so that Validate rejects it.
144	+const CloseReasonUnknown CloseReason = -1
145	+
146	+// CloseReasonTextMaxLength matches the VARCHAR(255) close_reason_text column, counted in characters.
147	+const CloseReasonTextMaxLength = 255
148	+
149	+// AllowedCloseReasons lists the reasons a person can pick when closing.
150	+// A pull request is completed by merging, so it cannot be closed as completed.
151	+func AllowedCloseReasons(isPull bool) []CloseReason {
152	+	if isPull {
153	+		return []CloseReason{CloseReasonNotPlanned, CloseReasonDuplicate, CloseReasonOther}
154	+	}
155	+	return []CloseReason{CloseReasonCompleted, CloseReasonNotPlanned, CloseReasonDuplicate, CloseReasonOther}
156	+}
157	+
158	+// CloseReasonOptions is the reason a person gives when closing an issue or pull request.
159	+type CloseReasonOptions struct {
160	+	Reason         CloseReason
161	+	Text           string // only for CloseReasonOther
162	+	DuplicateIndex int64  // only for CloseReasonDuplicate: the number of the issue it duplicates, in the same repository
163	+}
164	+
165	+// Validate checks the options for an issue or pull request, without looking anything up;
166	+// SetIssueAsClosed checks that the duplicate target exists.
167	+// CloseReasonNone is always valid, so close paths that give no reason keep working.
168	+func (opts CloseReasonOptions) Validate(isPull bool) error {
169	+	if opts.Reason != CloseReasonNone && !slices.Contains(AllowedCloseReasons(isPull), opts.Reason) {
170	+		return ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed{Reason: opts.Reason, IsPull: isPull}
171	+	}
172	+
173	+	if opts.Reason == CloseReasonDuplicate {
174	+		if opts.DuplicateIndex <= 0 {
175	+			return ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate{Index: opts.DuplicateIndex, Detail: "no issue number given"}
176	+		}
177	+	} else if opts.DuplicateIndex != 0 {
178	+		return ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate{Index: opts.DuplicateIndex, Detail: "an issue number is only allowed with the duplicate reason"}
179	+	}
180	+
181	+	hasText := strings.TrimSpace(opts.Text) != "" // whitespace-only counts as no text
182	+	if opts.Reason != CloseReasonOther {
183	+		if hasText {
184	+			return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: "text is only allowed with the other reason"}
185	+		}
186	+		return nil
187	+	}
188	+	if !hasText {
189	+		return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: "text is empty"}
190	+	}
191	+	if utf8.RuneCountInString(opts.Text) > CloseReasonTextMaxLength {
192	+		return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: fmt.Sprintf("text is longer than %d characters", CloseReasonTextMaxLength)}
193	+	}
194	+	return nil
195	+}
196	+
197	+// ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed represents a reason that is out of range, or not allowed for the issue or pull request.
198	+type ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed struct {
199	+	Reason CloseReason
200	+	IsPull bool
201	+}
202	+
203	+// IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed checks if an error is a ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed.
204	+func IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed(err error) bool {
205	+	_, ok := err.(ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed)
206	+	return ok
207	+}
208	+
209	+func (err ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed) Error() string {
210	+	return fmt.Sprintf("close reason is not allowed for this %s [reason: %d]", util.Iif(err.IsPull, "pull request", "issue"), err.Reason)
211	+}
212	+
213	+func (err ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed) Unwrap() error {
214	+	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
215	+}
216	+
217	+// ErrInvalidCloseReasonText represents close reason text that is empty, too long, or sent with a reason other than CloseReasonOther.
218	+type ErrInvalidCloseReasonText struct {
219	+	Reason CloseReason
220	+	Detail string
221	+}
222	+
223	+// IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText checks if an error is a ErrInvalidCloseReasonText.
224	+func IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText(err error) bool {
225	+	_, ok := err.(ErrInvalidCloseReasonText)
226	+	return ok
227	+}
228	+
229	+func (err ErrInvalidCloseReasonText) Error() string {
230	+	return fmt.Sprintf("invalid close reason text: %s [reason: %d]", err.Detail, err.Reason)
231	+}
232	+
233	+func (err ErrInvalidCloseReasonText) Unwrap() error {
234	+	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
235	+}
236	+
237	+// ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate represents a duplicate target that is missing, is the issue itself, or is not in the same repository.
238	+type ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate struct {
239	+	Index  int64
240	+	Detail string
241	+}
242	+
243	+// IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate checks if an error is a ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate.
244	+func IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate(err error) bool {
245	+	_, ok := err.(ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate)
246	+	return ok
247	+}
248	+
249	+func (err ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate) Error() string {
250	+	return fmt.Sprintf("invalid duplicate target: %s [index: %d]", err.Detail, err.Index)
251	+}
252	+
253	+func (err ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate) Unwrap() error {
254	+	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
255	+}

288	+	other.CloseReason = issues_model.CloseReasonOther
289	+	other.CloseReasonText = "superseded by a new design"
290	+	require.NoError(t, issues_model.UpdateIssueCols(t.Context(), other, "close_reason", "close_reason_text"))
291	+
292	+	duplicate := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 2})
293	+	duplicate.CloseReason = issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate
294	+	duplicate.CloseDuplicateIssueID = 1
295	+	require.NoError(t, issues_model.UpdateIssueCols(t.Context(), duplicate, "close_reason", "close_duplicate_issue_id"))
296	+
297	+	// reload and compare: bean conditions skip unmapped and zero-valued fields, so they can't catch a missing column
298	+	other = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
299	+	assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonOther, other.CloseReason)
300	+	assert.Equal(t, "superseded by a new design", other.CloseReasonText)
301	+
302	+	duplicate = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 2})
303	+	assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, duplicate.CloseReason)
304	+	assert.EqualValues(t, 1, duplicate.CloseDuplicateIssueID)
305	+}

321	+func TestCloseReasonOptionsValidate(t *testing.T) {
322	+	cases := []struct {
323	+		name   string
324	+		opts   issues_model.CloseReasonOptions
325	+		isPull bool
326	+		isErr  func(error) bool // nil when the options are valid
327	+	}{
328	+		{name: "no reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{}},
329	+		{name: "no reason on a pull request", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{}, isPull: true},
330	+		{name: "completed issue", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonCompleted}},
331	+		{name: "not planned pull request", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonNotPlanned}, isPull: true},
332	+		{name: "duplicate with a number", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, DuplicateIndex: 3}},
333	+		{name: "other with text", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: "superseded"}},
334	+		{name: "other with 255 two-byte characters", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: strings.Repeat("é", 255)}},
335	+		{name: "whitespace-only text with another reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonCompleted, Text: " "}},
336	+
337	+		{name: "completed pull request", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonCompleted}, isPull: true, isErr: issues_model.IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed},
338	+		{name: "out of range", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: 99}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed},
339	+		{name: "other with no text", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
340	+		{name: "other with whitespace-only text", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: " \t\n"}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
341	+		{name: "other with 256 characters", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: strings.Repeat("a", 256)}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
342	+		{name: "text with another reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonNotPlanned, Text: "because"}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
343	+		{name: "text with no reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Text: "because"}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
344	+		{name: "duplicate with no number", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate},
345	+		{name: "duplicate with a negative number", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, DuplicateIndex: -1}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate},
346	+		{name: "number with another reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonNotPlanned, DuplicateIndex: 3}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate},
347	+		{name: "number with no reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{DuplicateIndex: 3}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate},
348	+	}

395	+func TestCloseIssueInvalidReasonLeavesItOpen(t *testing.T) {
396	+	cases := []struct {

398	+		issueID int64
399	+		reason  issues_model.CloseReasonOptions
400	+		isErr   func(error) bool
401	+	}{

403	+		{name: "other with no text", issueID: 1, reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
404	+		{name: "duplicate of itself", issueID: 1, reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, DuplicateIndex: 1}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate},
405	+		{name: "duplicate of a number that does not exist", issueID: 1, reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, DuplicateIndex: 999}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate},
406	+		{name: "duplicate of a number only in another repository", issueID: 6, reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, DuplicateIndex: 3}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate}, // repo 3 has no #3; repo 1 does
407	+	}

410	+			require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())

412	+			doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
413	+
414	+			_, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(t.Context(), issue, doer, c.reason)
415	+			assert.True(t, c.isErr(err), "unexpected error: %v", err)
416	+			assert.False(t, issue.IsClosed, "the in-memory issue must not be changed either")
417	+
418	+			issue = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: c.issueID})
419	+			assert.False(t, issue.IsClosed)
420	+			assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonNone, issue.CloseReason)
421	+			unittest.AssertNotExistsBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{IssueID: c.issueID, Type: issues_model.CommentTypeClose})
422	+		})

426	+func TestCloseIssueAsDuplicate(t *testing.T) {
427	+	require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
428	+	issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
429	+	target := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{RepoID: issue.RepoID, Index: 4}) // closed, which is allowed
430	+	doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
431	+
432	+	comment, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(t.Context(), issue, doer, issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, DuplicateIndex: 4})
433	+	require.NoError(t, err)
434	+
435	+	issue = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
436	+	assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, issue.CloseReason)
437	+	assert.Equal(t, target.ID, issue.CloseDuplicateIssueID) // stored as the global ID, not the number
438	+
439	+	comment = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{ID: comment.ID})
440	+	assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, comment.MetaCloseReason().Reason)
441	+	require.NoError(t, comment.LoadCloseDuplicateIssue(t.Context()))
442	+	require.NotNil(t, comment.CloseDuplicateIssue)
443	+	assert.Equal(t, target.ID, comment.CloseDuplicateIssue.ID)
444	+	assert.Equal(t, int64(4), comment.CloseDuplicateIssue.Index)
445	+	assert.Equal(t, target.Title, comment.CloseDuplicateIssue.Title)
446	+	assert.True(t, strings.HasSuffix(comment.CloseDuplicateIssue.Link(), "/user2/repo1/issues/4"), comment.CloseDuplicateIssue.Link())
447	+}

456	+func TestReopenIssueClearsReason(t *testing.T) {
457	+	cases := []struct {
458	+		name   string
459	+		reason issues_model.CloseReasonOptions
460	+	}{
461	+		{name: "other with text", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: "superseded"}},
462	+		{name: "duplicate", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, DuplicateIndex: 4}},
463	+	}
464	+	for _, c := range cases {
465	+		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
466	+			require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
467	+			issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
468	+			doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
469	+
470	+			closeComment, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(t.Context(), issue, doer, c.reason)
471	+			require.NoError(t, err)
472	+			reopenComment, err := issues_model.ReopenIssue(t.Context(), issue, doer)
473	+			require.NoError(t, err)
474	+
475	+			issue = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
476	+			assert.False(t, issue.IsClosed)
477	+			assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonNone, issue.CloseReason)
478	+			assert.Empty(t, issue.CloseReasonText)
479	+			assert.Zero(t, issue.CloseDuplicateIssueID)
480	+
481	+			closeComment = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{ID: closeComment.ID})
482	+			assert.Equal(t, c.reason.Reason, closeComment.MetaCloseReason().Reason, "the close comment keeps its reason")
483	+			assert.Equal(t, c.reason.Text, closeComment.MetaCloseReason().Text)
484	+			require.NoError(t, closeComment.LoadCloseDuplicateIssue(t.Context()))
485	+			assert.Equal(t, c.reason.Reason == issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, closeComment.CloseDuplicateIssue != nil)
486	+
487	+			reopenComment = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{ID: reopenComment.ID})
488	+			assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CommentTypeReopen, reopenComment.Type)
489	+			assert.Nil(t, reopenComment.CommentMetaData)
490	+		})
491	+	}
492	+}

+	}

new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..c8cf8ef2c9
--- /dev/null
+++ b/models/issues/issue_close_reason.go
@@ -0,0 +1,139 @@
+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+package issues
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"slices"
+	"strings"
+	"unicode/utf8"
+
+	"gitea.dev/modules/util"
+)
+
+// CloseReason records why an issue or pull request was closed.
+// It is stored as an integer, so existing values must never be renumbered.
+type CloseReason int
+
+const (
+	CloseReasonNone       CloseReason = iota // 0
+	CloseReasonCompleted                     // 1
+	CloseReasonNotPlanned                    // 2
+	CloseReasonDuplicate                     // 3
+	CloseReasonOther                         // 4
+)
+
+// CloseReasonUnknown is never stored: it stands for an unrecognised reason name, so that Validate rejects it.
+const CloseReasonUnknown CloseReason = -1
+
+// CloseReasonTextMaxLength matches the VARCHAR(255) close_reason_text column, counted in characters.
+const CloseReasonTextMaxLength = 255
+
+// AllowedCloseReasons lists the reasons a person can pick when closing.
+// A pull request is completed by merging, so it cannot be closed as completed.
+func AllowedCloseReasons(isPull bool) []CloseReason {
+	if isPull {
+		return []CloseReason{CloseReasonNotPlanned, CloseReasonDuplicate, CloseReasonOther}
+	}
+	return []CloseReason{CloseReasonCompleted, CloseReasonNotPlanned, CloseReasonDuplicate, CloseReasonOther}
+}
+
+// CloseReasonOptions is the reason a person gives when closing an issue or pull request.
+type CloseReasonOptions struct {
+	Reason         CloseReason
+	Text           string // only for CloseReasonOther
+	DuplicateIndex int64  // only for CloseReasonDuplicate: the number of the issue it duplicates, in the same repository
+}
+
+// Validate checks the options for an issue or pull request, without looking anything up;
+// SetIssueAsClosed checks that the duplicate target exists.
+// CloseReasonNone is always valid, so close paths that give no reason keep working.
+func (opts CloseReasonOptions) Validate(isPull bool) error {
+	if opts.Reason != CloseReasonNone && !slices.Contains(AllowedCloseReasons(isPull), opts.Reason) {
+		return ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed{Reason: opts.Reason, IsPull: isPull}
+	}
+
+	if opts.Reason == CloseReasonDuplicate {
+		if opts.DuplicateIndex <= 0 {
+			return ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate{Index: opts.DuplicateIndex, Detail: "no issue number given"}
+		}
+	} else if opts.DuplicateIndex != 0 {
+		return ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate{Index: opts.DuplicateIndex, Detail: "an issue number is only allowed with the duplicate reason"}
+	}
+
+	hasText := strings.TrimSpace(opts.Text) != "" // whitespace-only counts as no text
+	if opts.Reason != CloseReasonOther {
+		if hasText {
+			return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: "text is only allowed with the other reason"}
+		}
+		return nil
+	}
+	if !hasText {
+		return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: "text is empty"}
+	}
+	if utf8.RuneCountInString(opts.Text) > CloseReasonTextMaxLength {
+		return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: fmt.Sprintf("text is longer than %d characters", CloseReasonTextMaxLength)}
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed represents a reason that is out of range, or not allowed for the issue or pull request.
+type ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed struct {
+	Reason CloseReason
+	IsPull bool
+}
+
+// IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed checks if an error is a ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed.
+func IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed(err error) bool {
+	_, ok := err.(ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed)
+	return ok
+}
+
+func (err ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed) Error() string {
+	return fmt.Sprintf("close reason is not allowed for this %s [reason: %d]", util.Iif(err.IsPull, "pull request", "issue"), err.Reason)
+}
+
+func (err ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed) Unwrap() error {
+	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
+}
+
+// ErrInvalidCloseReasonText represents close reason text that is empty, too long, or sent with a reason other than CloseReasonOther.
+type ErrInvalidCloseReasonText struct {
+	Reason CloseReason
+	Detail string
+}
+
+// IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText checks if an error is a ErrInvalidCloseReasonText.
+func IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText(err error) bool {
+	_, ok := err.(ErrInvalidCloseReasonText)
+	return ok
+}
+
+func (err ErrInvalidCloseReasonText) Error() string {
+	return fmt.Sprintf("invalid close reason text: %s [reason: %d]", err.Detail, err.Reason)
+}
+
+func (err ErrInvalidCloseReasonText) Unwrap() error {
+	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
+}
+
+// ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate represents a duplicate target that is missing, is the issue itself, or is not in the same repository.
+type ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate struct {
+	Index  int64
+	Detail string
+}
+
+// IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate checks if an error is a ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate.
+func IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate(err error) bool {
+	_, ok := err.(ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate)
+	return ok
+}
+
+func (err ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate) Error() string {
+	return fmt.Sprintf("invalid duplicate target: %s [index: %d]", err.Detail, err.Index)
+}
+
+func (err ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate) Unwrap() error {
+	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
+}

+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+package v1_27
+
+import (
+	"gitea.dev/models/db"
+
+	"xorm.io/xorm"
+)
+
+func AddCloseReasonToIssue(x db.EngineMigration) error {
+	type Issue struct {
+		CloseReason           int    `xorm:"SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"`
+		CloseReasonText       string `xorm:"VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL DEFAULT ''"`
+		CloseDuplicateIssueID int64  `xorm:"NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"`
+	}
+	_, err := x.SyncWithOptions(xorm.SyncOptions{
+		IgnoreDropIndices: true,
+		IgnoreConstrains:  true,
+	}, new(Issue))
+	return err
+}

+
+func Test_AddCloseReasonToIssue(t *testing.T) {
+	type Issue struct {
+		ID       int64 `xorm:"pk autoincr"`
+		RepoID   int64 `xorm:"INDEX UNIQUE(repo_index)"`
+		Index    int64 `xorm:"UNIQUE(repo_index)"`
+		IsClosed bool  `xorm:"INDEX"`
+		IsPull   bool  `xorm:"INDEX"`
+	}
+
+	x, deferable := migrationtest.PrepareTestEnv(t, 0, new(Issue))
+	defer deferable()
+
+	require.NoError(t, AddCloseReasonToIssue(x))
+
+	var issues []struct {
+		ID                    int64
+		CloseReason           int
+		CloseReasonText       string
+		CloseDuplicateIssueID int64
+	}
+	require.NoError(t, x.Table("issue").Asc("id").Find(&issues))
+	require.Len(t, issues, 4) // guards against the fixtures silently not loading
+	for _, issue := range issues {
+		assert.Zero(t, issue.CloseReason, "issue %d", issue.ID)
+		assert.Empty(t, issue.CloseReasonText, "issue %d", issue.ID)
+		assert.Zero(t, issue.CloseDuplicateIssueID, "issue %d", issue.ID)
+	}
+}

112	new file mode 100644
113	index 0000000000..c8cf8ef2c9
114	--- /dev/null
115	+++ b/models/issues/issue_close_reason.go
116	@@ -0,0 +1,139 @@
117	+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
118	+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
119	+
120	+package issues
121	+
122	+import (
123	+	"fmt"
124	+	"slices"
125	+	"strings"
126	+	"unicode/utf8"
127	+
128	+	"gitea.dev/modules/util"
129	+)
130	+
131	+// CloseReason records why an issue or pull request was closed.
132	+// It is stored as an integer, so existing values must never be renumbered.
133	+type CloseReason int
134	+
135	+const (
136	+	CloseReasonNone       CloseReason = iota // 0
137	+	CloseReasonCompleted                     // 1
138	+	CloseReasonNotPlanned                    // 2
139	+	CloseReasonDuplicate                     // 3
140	+	CloseReasonOther                         // 4
141	+)
142	+
143	+// CloseReasonUnknown is never stored: it stands for an unrecognised reason name, so that Validate rejects it.
144	+const CloseReasonUnknown CloseReason = -1
145	+
146	+// CloseReasonTextMaxLength matches the VARCHAR(255) close_reason_text column, counted in characters.
147	+const CloseReasonTextMaxLength = 255
148	+
149	+// AllowedCloseReasons lists the reasons a person can pick when closing.
150	+// A pull request is completed by merging, so it cannot be closed as completed.
151	+func AllowedCloseReasons(isPull bool) []CloseReason {
152	+	if isPull {
153	+		return []CloseReason{CloseReasonNotPlanned, CloseReasonDuplicate, CloseReasonOther}
154	+	}
155	+	return []CloseReason{CloseReasonCompleted, CloseReasonNotPlanned, CloseReasonDuplicate, CloseReasonOther}
156	+}
157	+
158	+// CloseReasonOptions is the reason a person gives when closing an issue or pull request.
159	+type CloseReasonOptions struct {
160	+	Reason         CloseReason
161	+	Text           string // only for CloseReasonOther
162	+	DuplicateIndex int64  // only for CloseReasonDuplicate: the number of the issue it duplicates, in the same repository
163	+}
164	+
165	+// Validate checks the options for an issue or pull request, without looking anything up;
166	+// SetIssueAsClosed checks that the duplicate target exists.
167	+// CloseReasonNone is always valid, so close paths that give no reason keep working.
168	+func (opts CloseReasonOptions) Validate(isPull bool) error {
169	+	if opts.Reason != CloseReasonNone && !slices.Contains(AllowedCloseReasons(isPull), opts.Reason) {
170	+		return ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed{Reason: opts.Reason, IsPull: isPull}
171	+	}
172	+
173	+	if opts.Reason == CloseReasonDuplicate {
174	+		if opts.DuplicateIndex <= 0 {
175	+			return ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate{Index: opts.DuplicateIndex, Detail: "no issue number given"}
176	+		}
177	+	} else if opts.DuplicateIndex != 0 {
178	+		return ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate{Index: opts.DuplicateIndex, Detail: "an issue number is only allowed with the duplicate reason"}
179	+	}
180	+
181	+	hasText := strings.TrimSpace(opts.Text) != "" // whitespace-only counts as no text
182	+	if opts.Reason != CloseReasonOther {
183	+		if hasText {
184	+			return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: "text is only allowed with the other reason"}
185	+		}
186	+		return nil
187	+	}
188	+	if !hasText {
189	+		return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: "text is empty"}
190	+	}
191	+	if utf8.RuneCountInString(opts.Text) > CloseReasonTextMaxLength {
192	+		return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: fmt.Sprintf("text is longer than %d characters", CloseReasonTextMaxLength)}
193	+	}
194	+	return nil
195	+}
196	+
197	+// ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed represents a reason that is out of range, or not allowed for the issue or pull request.
198	+type ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed struct {
199	+	Reason CloseReason
200	+	IsPull bool
201	+}
202	+
203	+// IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed checks if an error is a ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed.
204	+func IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed(err error) bool {
205	+	_, ok := err.(ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed)
206	+	return ok
207	+}
208	+
209	+func (err ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed) Error() string {
210	+	return fmt.Sprintf("close reason is not allowed for this %s [reason: %d]", util.Iif(err.IsPull, "pull request", "issue"), err.Reason)
211	+}
212	+
213	+func (err ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed) Unwrap() error {
214	+	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
215	+}
216	+
217	+// ErrInvalidCloseReasonText represents close reason text that is empty, too long, or sent with a reason other than CloseReasonOther.
218	+type ErrInvalidCloseReasonText struct {
219	+	Reason CloseReason
220	+	Detail string
221	+}
222	+
223	+// IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText checks if an error is a ErrInvalidCloseReasonText.
224	+func IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText(err error) bool {
225	+	_, ok := err.(ErrInvalidCloseReasonText)
226	+	return ok
227	+}
228	+
229	+func (err ErrInvalidCloseReasonText) Error() string {
230	+	return fmt.Sprintf("invalid close reason text: %s [reason: %d]", err.Detail, err.Reason)
231	+}
232	+
233	+func (err ErrInvalidCloseReasonText) Unwrap() error {
234	+	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
235	+}
236	+
237	+// ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate represents a duplicate target that is missing, is the issue itself, or is not in the same repository.
238	+type ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate struct {
239	+	Index  int64
240	+	Detail string
241	+}
242	+
243	+// IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate checks if an error is a ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate.
244	+func IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate(err error) bool {
245	+	_, ok := err.(ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate)
246	+	return ok
247	+}
248	+
249	+func (err ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate) Error() string {
250	+	return fmt.Sprintf("invalid duplicate target: %s [index: %d]", err.Detail, err.Index)
251	+}
252	+
253	+func (err ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate) Unwrap() error {
254	+	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
255	+}

299	+	assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonOther, other.CloseReason)

303	+	assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, duplicate.CloseReason)
304	+	assert.EqualValues(t, 1, duplicate.CloseDuplicateIssueID)

331	+		{name: "not planned pull request", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonNotPlanned}, isPull: true},

456	+func TestReopenIssueClearsReason(t *testing.T) {
457	+	cases := []struct {
458	+		name   string
459	+		reason issues_model.CloseReasonOptions
460	+	}{
461	+		{name: "other with text", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: "superseded"}},
462	+		{name: "duplicate", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, DuplicateIndex: 4}},
463	+	}
464	+	for _, c := range cases {
465	+		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
466	+			require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
467	+			issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
468	+			doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
469	+
470	+			closeComment, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(t.Context(), issue, doer, c.reason)
471	+			require.NoError(t, err)
472	+			reopenComment, err := issues_model.ReopenIssue(t.Context(), issue, doer)
473	+			require.NoError(t, err)
474	+
475	+			issue = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
476	+			assert.False(t, issue.IsClosed)
477	+			assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonNone, issue.CloseReason)
478	+			assert.Empty(t, issue.CloseReasonText)
479	+			assert.Zero(t, issue.CloseDuplicateIssueID)
480	+
481	+			closeComment = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{ID: closeComment.ID})
482	+			assert.Equal(t, c.reason.Reason, closeComment.MetaCloseReason().Reason, "the close comment keeps its reason")
483	+			assert.Equal(t, c.reason.Text, closeComment.MetaCloseReason().Text)
484	+			require.NoError(t, closeComment.LoadCloseDuplicateIssue(t.Context()))
485	+			assert.Equal(t, c.reason.Reason == issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, closeComment.CloseDuplicateIssue != nil)
486	+
487	+			reopenComment = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{ID: reopenComment.ID})
488	+			assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CommentTypeReopen, reopenComment.Type)
489	+			assert.Nil(t, reopenComment.CommentMetaData)
490	+		})
491	+	}
492	+}

 # models/db — engine access, transactions and generic queries
@@ -45,6 +45,11 @@ registration.
 - **Never call `x.Update(exemplar)` without an explicit `WHERE`** — it updates every row
   (`docs/guidelines-backend.md`).
 - Fields tagged `xorm:"-"` are in-memory only. They are never read from or written to the database.
+- An enum column is a named Go integer type with `iota` constants, stored as a plain integer column:
+  `CommentType` (`models/issues/comment.go`), `XRefAction` (`modules/references/references.go`,
+  tagged `SMALLINT`). No model uses a database `ENUM`. The database holds only the numbers, so
+  existing values are never renumbered, and nothing but Go code rejects an out-of-range value.
+  Commit status `State` (`models/git/commit_status.go`) is the string-typed exception.

120	+package issues

123	+	"fmt"
124	+	"slices"
125	+	"strings"
126	+	"unicode/utf8"
127	+
128	+	"gitea.dev/modules/util"
129	+)
130	+
131	+// CloseReason records why an issue or pull request was closed.
132	+// It is stored as an integer, so existing values must never be renumbered.
133	+type CloseReason int
134	+
135	+const (
136	+	CloseReasonNone       CloseReason = iota // 0
137	+	CloseReasonCompleted                     // 1
138	+	CloseReasonNotPlanned                    // 2
139	+	CloseReasonDuplicate                     // 3
140	+	CloseReasonOther                         // 4
141	+)
142	+
143	+// CloseReasonUnknown is never stored: it stands for an unrecognised reason name, so that Validate rejects it.
144	+const CloseReasonUnknown CloseReason = -1
145	+
146	+// CloseReasonTextMaxLength matches the VARCHAR(255) close_reason_text column, counted in characters.
147	+const CloseReasonTextMaxLength = 255
148	+
149	+// AllowedCloseReasons lists the reasons a person can pick when closing.
150	+// A pull request is completed by merging, so it cannot be closed as completed.
151	+func AllowedCloseReasons(isPull bool) []CloseReason {
152	+	if isPull {
153	+		return []CloseReason{CloseReasonNotPlanned, CloseReasonDuplicate, CloseReasonOther}
154	+	}
155	+	return []CloseReason{CloseReasonCompleted, CloseReasonNotPlanned, CloseReasonDuplicate, CloseReasonOther}
156	+}
157	+
158	+// CloseReasonOptions is the reason a person gives when closing an issue or pull request.
159	+type CloseReasonOptions struct {
160	+	Reason         CloseReason
161	+	Text           string // only for CloseReasonOther
162	+	DuplicateIndex int64  // only for CloseReasonDuplicate: the number of the issue it duplicates, in the same repository
163	+}
164	+
165	+// Validate checks the options for an issue or pull request, without looking anything up;
166	+// SetIssueAsClosed checks that the duplicate target exists.
167	+// CloseReasonNone is always valid, so close paths that give no reason keep working.
168	+func (opts CloseReasonOptions) Validate(isPull bool) error {
169	+	if opts.Reason != CloseReasonNone && !slices.Contains(AllowedCloseReasons(isPull), opts.Reason) {
170	+		return ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed{Reason: opts.Reason, IsPull: isPull}
171	+	}
172	+
173	+	if opts.Reason == CloseReasonDuplicate {
174	+		if opts.DuplicateIndex <= 0 {
175	+			return ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate{Index: opts.DuplicateIndex, Detail: "no issue number given"}
176	+		}
177	+	} else if opts.DuplicateIndex != 0 {
178	+		return ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate{Index: opts.DuplicateIndex, Detail: "an issue number is only allowed with the duplicate reason"}
179	+	}
180	+
181	+	hasText := strings.TrimSpace(opts.Text) != "" // whitespace-only counts as no text
182	+	if opts.Reason != CloseReasonOther {
183	+		if hasText {
184	+			return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: "text is only allowed with the other reason"}
185	+		}
186	+		return nil
187	+	}
188	+	if !hasText {
189	+		return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: "text is empty"}
190	+	}
191	+	if utf8.RuneCountInString(opts.Text) > CloseReasonTextMaxLength {
192	+		return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: fmt.Sprintf("text is longer than %d characters", CloseReasonTextMaxLength)}
193	+	}
194	+	return nil
195	+}
196	+

280	+func TestIssueCloseReasonPersists(t *testing.T) {
281	+	require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
282	+
283	+	other := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
284	+	assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonNone, other.CloseReason) // fixtures set no reason, so this is the column default
285	+	assert.Empty(t, other.CloseReasonText)
286	+	assert.Zero(t, other.CloseDuplicateIssueID)
287	+
288	+	other.CloseReason = issues_model.CloseReasonOther
289	+	other.CloseReasonText = "superseded by a new design"
290	+	require.NoError(t, issues_model.UpdateIssueCols(t.Context(), other, "close_reason", "close_reason_text"))
291	+
292	+	duplicate := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 2})
293	+	duplicate.CloseReason = issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate
294	+	duplicate.CloseDuplicateIssueID = 1
295	+	require.NoError(t, issues_model.UpdateIssueCols(t.Context(), duplicate, "close_reason", "close_duplicate_issue_id"))
296	+
297	+	// reload and compare: bean conditions skip unmapped and zero-valued fields, so they can't catch a missing column
298	+	other = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
299	+	assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonOther, other.CloseReason)
300	+	assert.Equal(t, "superseded by a new design", other.CloseReasonText)
301	+
302	+	duplicate = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 2})
303	+	assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, duplicate.CloseReason)
304	+	assert.EqualValues(t, 1, duplicate.CloseDuplicateIssueID)
305	+}

321	+func TestCloseReasonOptionsValidate(t *testing.T) {
322	+	cases := []struct {
323	+		name   string
324	+		opts   issues_model.CloseReasonOptions
325	+		isPull bool
326	+		isErr  func(error) bool // nil when the options are valid
327	+	}{
328	+		{name: "no reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{}},
329	+		{name: "no reason on a pull request", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{}, isPull: true},
330	+		{name: "completed issue", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonCompleted}},
331	+		{name: "not planned pull request", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonNotPlanned}, isPull: true},
332	+		{name: "duplicate with a number", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, DuplicateIndex: 3}},
333	+		{name: "other with text", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: "superseded"}},
334	+		{name: "other with 255 two-byte characters", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: strings.Repeat("é", 255)}},
335	+		{name: "whitespace-only text with another reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonCompleted, Text: " "}},
336	+
337	+		{name: "completed pull request", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonCompleted}, isPull: true, isErr: issues_model.IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed},
338	+		{name: "out of range", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: 99}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed},
339	+		{name: "other with no text", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
340	+		{name: "other with whitespace-only text", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: " \t\n"}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
341	+		{name: "other with 256 characters", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: strings.Repeat("a", 256)}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
342	+		{name: "text with another reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonNotPlanned, Text: "because"}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
343	+		{name: "text with no reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Text: "because"}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
344	+		{name: "duplicate with no number", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate},
345	+		{name: "duplicate with a negative number", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, DuplicateIndex: -1}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate},
346	+		{name: "number with another reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonNotPlanned, DuplicateIndex: 3}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate},
347	+		{name: "number with no reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{DuplicateIndex: 3}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate},
348	+	}
349	+	for _, c := range cases {
350	+		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
351	+			err := c.opts.Validate(c.isPull)
352	+			if c.isErr == nil {
353	+				assert.NoError(t, err)
354	+				return
355	+			}
356	+			assert.True(t, c.isErr(err), "unexpected error: %v", err)
357	+			assert.ErrorIs(t, err, util.ErrInvalidArgument)
358	+		})
359	+	}
360	+}

362	+func TestCloseIssueRecordsReason(t *testing.T) {
363	+	cases := []struct {
364	+		name     string
365	+		reason   issues_model.CloseReasonOptions
366	+		wantText string
367	+	}{
368	+		{name: "no reason", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{}},
369	+		{name: "completed", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonCompleted}},
370	+		{name: "other with text", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: "superseded"}, wantText: "superseded"},
371	+		{name: "other text is stored as entered", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: "  superseded by #4  "}, wantText: "  superseded by #4  "},
372	+		{name: "whitespace-only text is not stored", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonNotPlanned, Text: " "}},
373	+	}
374	+	for _, c := range cases {
375	+		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
376	+			require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
377	+			issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
378	+			doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
379	+
380	+			comment, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(t.Context(), issue, doer, c.reason)
381	+			require.NoError(t, err)
382	+
383	+			want := issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: c.reason.Reason, Text: c.wantText}
384	+			issue = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
385	+			assert.True(t, issue.IsClosed)
386	+			assert.Equal(t, want, issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issue.CloseReason, Text: issue.CloseReasonText})
387	+
388	+			comment = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{ID: comment.ID}) // reloaded, so the metadata went through JSON
389	+			assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CommentTypeClose, comment.Type)
390	+			assert.Equal(t, want, comment.MetaCloseReason())
391	+		})
392	+	}
393	+}

395	+func TestCloseIssueInvalidReasonLeavesItOpen(t *testing.T) {
396	+	cases := []struct {
397	+		name    string
398	+		issueID int64
399	+		reason  issues_model.CloseReasonOptions
400	+		isErr   func(error) bool
401	+	}{
402	+		{name: "pull request closed as completed", issueID: 2, reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonCompleted}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed},
403	+		{name: "other with no text", issueID: 1, reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
404	+		{name: "duplicate of itself", issueID: 1, reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, DuplicateIndex: 1}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate},
405	+		{name: "duplicate of a number that does not exist", issueID: 1, reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, DuplicateIndex: 999}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate},
406	+		{name: "duplicate of a number only in another repository", issueID: 6, reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, DuplicateIndex: 3}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate}, // repo 3 has no #3; repo 1 does
407	+	}
408	+	for _, c := range cases {
409	+		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
410	+			require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
411	+			issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: c.issueID})
412	+			doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
413	+
414	+			_, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(t.Context(), issue, doer, c.reason)
415	+			assert.True(t, c.isErr(err), "unexpected error: %v", err)
416	+			assert.False(t, issue.IsClosed, "the in-memory issue must not be changed either")
417	+
418	+			issue = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: c.issueID})
419	+			assert.False(t, issue.IsClosed)
420	+			assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonNone, issue.CloseReason)
421	+			unittest.AssertNotExistsBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{IssueID: c.issueID, Type: issues_model.CommentTypeClose})
422	+		})
423	+	}
424	+}
